Content: A US infantryman pauses during the 1945 push into Germany to read his copy of the Stars & Stripes.Photograph: APView image in fullscreenA US infantryman pauses during the 1945 push into Germany to read his copy of the Stars & Stripes.Photograph: APUS militaryThree journalists sue Pentagon after being fired from military news outletThree employees of Stars and Stripes, a government-funded news service, allege they were fired after reporting on USS Abraham LincolnRobert MackeyThu 27 Aug 2026 19.33 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 19.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThree journalists who werefired by the Pentagonfrom a US government-funded news outlet sued the Department of Defense in federal court on Thursday, arguing their dismissals were illegal and violated their first amendment rights to free speech.The three journalists were all employees of Stars and Stripes, whichtheir court filingcalls “the U.S. military’s independent news source since the Civil War with a long history of editorial independence, free from news management or censorship by military command”.Max Lederer, the news outlet’s former publisher Max Lederer, Erik Slavin, the editor-in-chief, and Lara Korte, Middle East correspondent, allege the defense department and Pete Hegseth, the defense secretary, “are attempting to fire Plaintiffs for speaking up as private citizens in support of the press’s freedom to cover military operations, its need to reach all servicepersons, and in retaliation for their publication of a news report on deteriorating conditions aboard the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln during its extended tour of duty in the Mid-East”.Slavin and Korte said they were dismissed for supposed “insubordination” during an interview with CBS News in which they objected to potential censorship by theUS military. According to the complaint, no one at the Pentagon took “immediate action” after the interview aired on 5 July.“After all, the anodyne statements endorsing Stripes’ editorial independence were entirely consistent with DoD’s own longstanding insistence on Stripes’ independence,” reads the complaint.The journalists allege that “the spark that moved [the Pentagon] to act” was an 11 August news report about the conditions on the troubledUSS Abraham Lincoln, which had been supporting US military operations in the middle east for nearly nine months.“The article broke a major story about deteriorating conditions aboard the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln,” the complaint says. “It reported that the aircraft carrier’s 5,000 Sailors have endured food and water shortages, disrupted mail service, long workdays, and little time off for months on end, and that the long deployment and physical hardships were impacting Sailors’ physical and mental health”.The day afterthat articlewas published by Stars and Stripes, the suit contends, Lederer was ordered to fire Slavin and Korte – five and a half weeks after the CBS News interview. Lederer ultimately declined to comply with the order.“Lederer did not deliver the notices,” the suit explains. “Instead, he decided then and there to retire, and informed the Stripes’ staff via email. Mr. Lederer took this step because he did not want to be part of Defendants’ scheme to illegally punish Mr. Slavin and Ms. Korte for exercising their First Amendment rights.”Lederer was dismissed shortly after announcing his impending retirement, effective at the end of September. He said the Pentagon had installed a new deputy publisher, an active duty service member, under him at the newspaper without his prior knowledge.“Stripes’ historical editorial independence is critical to its core mission of gathering and providing unbiased, credible journalism to the U.S. military community, particularly servicemembers and their families stationed overseas,” the suit also says.The Pentagon did not immediately return a request for comment on Thursday’s lawsuit.Explore more on these topicsUS militarynewsShareReuse this content

title: Democrats to investigate ‘miraculous’ rise of Trump Jr’s investment firm | Donald Trump Jr | The Guardian
description: Congressman Jamie Raskin asks president’s son to detail firm’s recent success after he joined 1789 Capital as partner
Author: Shrai Popat
Headline: Congressman Jamie Raskin asks president’s son to detail firm’s recent success after he joined 1789 Capital as partner
Content: Donald Trump Jr speaks during preparations for the second day of the Republican national convention in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on 16 July 2024.Photograph: Andrew Harnik/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDonald Trump Jr speaks during preparations for the second day of the Republican national convention in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on 16 July 2024.Photograph: Andrew Harnik/Getty ImagesDonald Trump JrDemocrats to investigate ‘miraculous’ rise of Trump Jr’s investment firmCongressman Jamie Raskin asks president’s son to detail firm’s recent success after he joined 1789 Capital as partnerShrai Popatin WashingtonThu 27 Aug 2026 16.33 EDTFirst published on Thu 27 Aug 2026 15.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDemocratson a powerful US congressional committee have launched an investigation into a venture capital firm which has thrived since recruiting Donald Trump’s son.Donald Trump Jrjoined 1789 Capital as a partner just days after his father won a second term in office in November 2024. Congressman Jamie Raskin, ranking member of the US House of Representatives judiciary committee, has asked the president’s son to detail the firm’s recent success.The Guardian previously reported that after Trump Jr joined 1789 Capital, its assets under management ballooned: going from a reported $150m in 2024, to$1bn last August, to $2.7bn at year’s end, to areported$3.5bn by May, according to SEC filings.A significant proportion of that capital came from foreign investors, according toCNN reportingand the Guardian’s review of SEC filings. Forty per cent of assets under management were from overseas investors.In a letterto the US president’s son, and the founders of the firm – Omeed Malik and Christopher Buskirk – judiciary committee Democrats have asked for records that include companies that have received investments from the firm and any communications with any US elected official or federal government officials by 9 September. However, in the minority, Democrats have little subpoena power without Republican support for their cause.“Two years ago,” Raskin wrote, 1789 Capital was “a struggling venture capital firm that earned consistently disappointing results by serially investing in total market flops” but has since undergone a “miraculous transformation”.“With Don Jr’s new leadership role, 1789 Capital has developed an uncanny ability to identify companies that are about to receive massive influxes of cash from theTrump administrationor to benefit from significant changes in federal policies and regulations,” the top Democrat wrote. “They say there is no such thing as a sure thing in investing, but this is about as close as you can get.”In a statement to the Guardian, AJ Merton, counsel for 1789 Capital, called the allegations leveled by Democrats “unsubstantiated talking points”.“Repackaging press clippings on congressional letterhead does not turn news headlines into evidence,” he added. “And that practice is a hallmark of partisan stunts and politically motivated harassment, not oversight.”Raskin also argued “it is now impossible to believe” that the firm’s “astonishing growth and success are due to anything other than insider political influence and thoroughgoing corruption”.The ranking member outlined a series of reports of recent investments by 1789 Capital that include millions of dollars in Vulcan Elements, a rare earth company, in August 2025. Before this, the manufacturer had reportedly touted several government contracts they had secured months prior. Raskin then notes that the Pentagon announced a $620m direct loan to Vulcan Elements in November last year. At the same time, the Department of Commerce (DoC) provided the company with a $50m grant under the Chips and Science Act – legislation signed by former president Joe Biden.“This was an amazing turn of events when the Trump Administration decided to pump over half a billion dollars into an unproven startup company,” Raskin wrote.He also pointed to a recent Julyinterview with CNBCin which the US president said that his children have “inside information” due to the fact his policies touch nearly every part of the economy.“I tell my kids, ‘stay away,’” Trump said at the time. “But they also have a life. You know, they were doing business long before I ever thought of running for president.”Inan interview with the New York Timeslast month, Trump Jr said he only talks to his father, the president, “every few weeks”, and never discusses business with him and – as a private citizen – holds “no policy position and no role within the administration whatsoever”.Raskin’s letter also citesreporting from the Guardianthat Anduril Inudstries, a major military contractor founded by Trump ally and donor Palmer Luckey, has received billions in government contracts over the last year. 1789 Capital, the judiciary Democrats note, has acquired a stake in the company. Anduril says in Trump’s first year in office it doubled its revenue – a growth rate of 100%.Earlier this month, theGuardian also reportedthat two appointments to the Defense Policy Board, a key Pentagon advisory body, include two men with ties to 1789 Capital.Andreessen Horowitz, one of Silicon Valley’s largest venture capital firms, co-invests in three defense contractors alongside Trump Jr’s firm. The other appointee, Blake Masters, also sits on the boards of three ventures tied to 1789 Capital.Both men now advise the Pentagon on the defense-technology sector those companies operate in.Explore more on these topicsDonald Trump JrTrump administrationDonald TrumpUS politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: CEOs earn 614 times more than workers at US’s 100 lowest-paying corporations | US income inequality | The Guardian
description: Analysis by Institute for Policy Studies found that between 2019 and 2025, CEO compensation increased 41.4%
Author: Michael Sainato
Headline: Analysis by Institute for Policy Studies found that between 2019 and 2025, CEO compensation increased 41.4%
Content: The wealth of at least 36 billionaires is linked to these low-wage 100 corporations, including Jeff Bezos.Photograph: Miguel J Rodriguez Carrillo/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe wealth of at least 36 billionaires is linked to these low-wage 100 corporations, including Jeff Bezos.Photograph: Miguel J Rodriguez Carrillo/AFP/Getty ImagesUS income inequalityCEOs earn 614 times more than workers at US’s 100 lowest-paying corporationsAnalysis by Institute for Policy Studies found that between 2019 and 2025, CEO compensation increased 41.4%Michael SainatoThu 27 Aug 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 13.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe average CEO of the US’s 100 largest, lowest-paying corporations earned 614 times more than their average worker last year, according to an analysis by the Institute for Policy Studies (IPS).IPS’s latest executive excessreportanalyzed compensation at the 100 S&P 500 corporations with the lowest median worker pay. Between 2019 and 2025, CEO compensation increased 41.4%, unadjusted for inflation, twice as much as the median worker pay increased at these firms during the same period, at 20.7%.Inflation also outpaced worker pay increases, rising by 25.9%.The CEO-to-worker pay ratio at the low-wage 100 firms increased 8.4% between 2019 and 2025.The average CEO compensation among low-wage 100 corporations was $17.5m in 2025, compared with median worker pay of $36,571.The wealth of at least 36 billionaires is linked to these low-wage 100 corporations, including Walmart’s eight Walton family members, Amazon’s Jeff Bezos and Mackenzie Scott, and Carvana co-founders Ernie Garcia II and Ernie Garcia III.“This is really a big problem for society, that we have such extremes,” said Sarah Anderson, lead author of the report and director of the Global Economy Project at the Institute for Policy Studies.A bar chart showing the largest CEO-to-worker pay ratios in the S&P 500“To me, it seems like these CEOs are just living on a remote economic planet from the one that their employees are living on, and it makes it really hard for them to fathom what it’s like to have to worry about putting food on your family’s table or even coming home at night if you are at risk of being detained by ICE.”The report notes that the low-wage 100 corporations have a combined force of 1,282 registered federal lobbyists and that many of these companies did not denounce aggressive immigration enforcement actions toward their workforce or on their property.“Low-wage workers are now facing the biggest cuts to Medicaid and Snap [food benefits] in history. Many of the employees at these companies have to rely on those programs, and then so many of them have also been terrorized and detained by ICE agents,” added Anderson. “So it’s really astounding that the leaders of these companies have turned a blind eye to this surge of threats against many of their workers, and instead they’ve just continue to be fixated on enriching themselves.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFirst ThingOur US morning briefing breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it mattersEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionStock buybacks among these firms increased in 2025, to $108.6bn from $105bn in 2024. Between 2019 and 2025, the low-wage 100 firms spent $718bn on stock buybacks.Among the 100 low-wage firms, Walmart spent the most on stock buybacks, at $8.1bn, equivalent to a $3,851 bonus to each of the company’s 2.1 million workers. Walmart’s CEO, Doug McMillan, who stepped down in January 2026, received $29.2m in compensation in 2025, 958 times more than the median worker pay at Walmart of $30,520.The report cites several policy solutions to excessive executive pay at corporations, including a tax hike on corporations that pay CEOs more than 50 times what they pay their median employees, an increase on stock buyback taxes and leveraging government contracts and subsidies to bar contractors from engaging in stock buybacks.Walmart did not respond to multiple requests for comment.Explore more on these topicsUS income inequalitynewsShareReuse this content

title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Liverpool need midfield nous, Michael Carrick is already under pressure and Villa can bid farewell to Enzi Konsa
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Liverpool need midfield nous, Michael Carrick is already under pressure and Villa can bid farewell to Enzi Konsa
Content: Left to right: Arsenal’s Ezri Konsa, Manchester City’s Marc Guéhi and Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White.Composite: EPA, GettyView image in fullscreenLeft to right: Arsenal’s Ezri Konsa, Manchester City’s Marc Guéhi and Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White.Composite: EPA, GettyTen things to look out for this weekendPremier LeaguePremier League: 10 things to look out for this weekendLiverpool need midfield nous, Michael Carrick is already under pressure and Villa can bid farewell to Enzi KonsaGuardian sportThu 27 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 19.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1Guéhi versatility crucial as Bouaddi arrivesEnzo Maresca hasa shiny new £85m midfielderhe could select for a debut but, at 18 years old, he may want Ayyoub Bouaddi to have a bit of time watching on from the bench to learn about the Premier League from his elders. The Moroccan may not have anticipated one of those to be a centre-back by trade. Marc Guéhi will be eager to make a triumphant return to Crystal Palace and may well have the opportunity to do so from central midfield, where he played last weekend in the victory over Bournemouth, scoring the equaliser. The centre-back was a surprise selection in the blocker role next to Elliot Anderson, but equipped himself admirably and was not limited to the dirty work, often being found in more advanced positions in open play and happy to have the ball at his feet. His long-term future is unlikely to be outside of defence but further proof of Guéhi’s adaptability will be a positive for Maresca, as a long season awaits.Will UnwinCrystal Palace vManchester City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)2Liverpool need to stop Gibbs-White“It is just not personnel,” insisted Andoni Iraola in response to Liverpool conceding two goals to quick Newcastle transitions in his first Premier League game as the club’s head coach. Some long-term faults can not be rectified overnight – although that did not prevent some hysterical reactions to the performance at St James’ Park – and with Liverpool prioritising wingers in the final days of the transfer window the answer to this particular weakness, as Iraola indicated, lies on the training ground. Morgan Gibbs-White revelled in the spaces behind Liverpool’s midfield last season as he – and set-pieces – helped Nottingham Forest toa second successive league win at Anfield. Iraola does not want to curb Ryan Gravenberch’s attacking instincts but greater tactical discipline and willingness to do the dirty work from the entire Liverpool midfield will be needed to stop Gibbs-White producing a repeat performance. Forest’snew record signing, Liam Delap, has also been registered in time to play.Andy HunterLiverpool vNottingham Forest, Saturday 12.30pm3Everton note Cherries’ set-piece strugglesThere were so many encouraging takeaways for Bournemouth despite an agonising late defeat at Manchester City. The catalyst for City’s turnaround was Marc Guéhi’s 84th-minute equaliser, the England defender heading in unmarked at a corner, after wasting a near-identical earlier chance. For Bournemouth, it was a familiar source of pain; only Liverpool conceded more set-piece goals in the top flight last season (20), with the Cherries and Crystal Palace both conceding 18. Bournemouth sought to address their vulnerability in the summer by hiring their first dedicated set-piece coach in Nicolas Gagnon, who worked with Canada at the World Cup and previously at Southampton and in Saudi Arabia. Only Arsenal, Manchester City,Manchester Unitedand Aston Villa claimed more points away from home than Everton last season and David Moyes’s centre-backs, Jarrad Branthwaite and James Tarkowski, will be licking their lips if Bournemouth do not sharpen up their act.Ben FisherBournemouth v Everton, Saturday 3pmView image in fullscreenBournemouth were again undone by a set-piece goal as they lost 2-1 at Manchester City.Photograph: Darren Staples/AFP/Getty Images4Too early for a relegation six-pointer?Contrasting opening weekends for Coventry and Hull, harsh reality dealt out against the dream scenario lived out. AtArsenal, Coventry were well beaten by the champions, while in East Yorkshire, Manchester United were soundly, deservedly defeated. Despite contrasting starts, both teams remain warm favourites for relegation. Two defeats in a row for Frank Lampard’s team would dim the optimism of a summer of anticipation. Hull seek to extend the reverie of last week though Coventry are unlikely to be caught as cold as United last week, and surely cannot defend set pieces so badly. The last three Championship matches between these two teams ended in draws, last season’s meetings goalless, although both squads have since been upgraded by brisk transfer business. At Hull, much is expected of Lucas Herrington who missed Australia’s fateful penalty against Egypt at the World Cup. The teenage defender shone against Stoke in the Tigers’ successful midweek Carabao Cup assignment.John BrewinCoventry v Hull, Saturday 3pm5Tottenham keen for Tonali to tickIt has not taken long for Sandro Tonali to be reunited with his former teammates. After succumbing 3-0 on the opening weekend atBrentford, a home victory will be the minimum requirement for Tottenham. Roberto De Zerbi and his players will be desperate to show that things have changed after a busy summer in the transfer market. Tonali will be a key part of that; he was the only central midfielder who made it past half-time in west London, so at least has minutes in his legs to build on. The Italian will be eager to not suffer at the hands of a team that served him well after bringing him to England. Tonali is supposed to make his new team tick and a rousing home debut would do a lot for everyone’s confidence, while defeat will bring plenty more questions.WUTottenham v Newcastle, Saturday 5.30pmView image in fullscreenSandro Tonali (left) faces his old club Newcastle after a difficult debut against Brentford.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian6Acheampong fights to stay with BluesThis is an important moment in Josh Acheampong’s development. The 20-year-old academy graduate did not have many opportunities last year but he started in Xabi Alonso’s back three whenChelseabeat Fulham on Monday. It was a big vote of confidence from Alonso in the young defender, who played well, and may indicate that Acheampong will stay at Stamford Bridge this season. Several clubs are interested in the England youth international and there is talk of a loan before the transfer window shuts, but Acheampong would strengthen his position further if he is selected again for Sunday’s home game against Brighton.Jacob Steinbergskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionChelsea v Brighton, Sunday 2pm7Carragher comments can fuel Black CatsOn Monday night, Jamie Carragher told a Sky Sports audience that he thought Sunderland might be relegated this season. The former Liverpool defender compared Régis Le Bris’s team to the Sheffield United side managed by Chris Wilder that went down in 2020-2021 – their second season after promotion – and suggested Sunderland were “arrogant”. How will Le Bris’s players respond against Fulham at the Stadium of Light on Sunday? Has the moment arrived to end a winlessPremier Leaguerun against the west London side stretching back 12 years? If there are legitimate concerns about the ability of Le Bris’s players to cope with a Europa League campaign, regular Sunderland watchers struggle to buy into the accusations or arrogance, let alone the analogy with a very different Sheffield United side. Nonetheless, last Saturday’s 2-1 defeat at Ipswich has prompted a certain anxiety, leaving Wearsiders hoping Nordi Mukiele is fit enough to raise defensive standards.Louise TaylorSunderland v Fulham, Sunday 2pmView image in fullscreenSunderland fans have bristled at Jamie Carragher’s prediction for their team’s season.Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters8Leeds look to strengthen as Bees buzzSub-plots abound at Elland Road as Leeds and Brentford meet after two wins apiece from their first competitive matches of the season. There is the goalkeeping beauty contest between Daniel Farke’s showpiece summer signing, James Trafford – who has registered two clean sheets in his opening games – and Brentford’s Caoimhin Kelleher. Further forward, fans can ponder the question of which centre forward, the Leeds favourite Dominic Calvert-Lewin or his opposite number Igor Thiago will prove the more incisive. Similarly the technical area tactical duel involving Daniel Farke and Keith Andrews looks extremely hard to call. Away from the pitch, Farke is hoping to win a race with Sunderland to sign Marseille winger Igor Paixão for around £30m as the Leeds manager urges his board to strengthen. “I’m happy with my group and my signings so far,” said Farke. “But we know we can definitely improve our squad. That is what Leeds supporters andLeeds Uniteddeserve.”LTLeeds v Brentford, Sunday 2pm9Carrick under pressure to deliverManchester United are bloody-nosed andIpswich Towndefinitely delighted after the tale of each team’s results on the opening weekend. At Hull City, Michael Carrick’s team played with zero cohesion and conviction and went down to a miserable 2-0 loss. At Portman Road Gary O’Neil’s side hosted Sunderland and claimed a rousing late 2-1 win, so arrive at Old Trafford with a bounce in the step. Carrick has to lift his men and get a result – preferably victory. A loss, at home, to another promoted team, would begin the latest inquest into a United No 1: a predicament suffered by every manager post-Sir Alex Ferguson.Jamie JacksonManchester United v Ipswich, Sunday 4.30pm10Villa fans bid farewell to KonsaAt a time when the manner of a player’s departure feels particularly pertinent, especially atAston Villa, Ezri Konsa can expect a warm reception on his return to the club. Konsa could make his Arsenal debut at Villa Park against his former club, where he excelled across seven seasons. A £12m buy from Brentford in 2019, Konsa surely represents one of their finest signings in the Premier League era. He joined fresh from a single season in the Championship with Brentford and left as an England regular and Europa League winner. Konsa’s role in Villa’s recent success should not be overlooked. Unai Emery can be judged by Villa’s extraordinary run of league finishes – seventh, fourth, sixth and fourth – but also his track record of turning promising talents, like Konsa, into fully-fledged internationals.BFAston Villa v Arsenal, Monday 8pmPosTeamPGDPts1Brighton1432Arsenal1333Brentford1334Everton1235Hull1236Chelsea1137Ipswich1138Man City1139Leeds11310Liverpool10111Newcastle10112Fulham1-1013AFC Bournemouth1-1014Sunderland1-1015Nottm Forest1-1016Crystal Palace1-2017Man Utd1-2018Coventry1-3019Tottenham Hotspur1-3020Aston Villa1-40Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueTen things to look out for this weekendArsenalManchester CityManchester UnitedTottenham HotspurLiverpoolChelseafeaturesShareReuse this content

title: WNBA star Brink launches withering attack on Kanter Freedom over anti-trans stunt | WNBA | The Guardian
description: The Los Angeles star defended the trans community and branded Freedom’s attempts to enter the WNBA draft as efforts to ‘stay relevant’
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: The Los Angeles star defended the trans community and branded Freedom’s attempts to enter the WNBA draft as efforts to ‘stay relevant’
Content: Cameron Brink has played for the Los Angeles Sparks since 2024.Photograph: Catalina Fragoso/NBAE/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCameron Brink has played for the Los Angeles Sparks since 2024.Photograph: Catalina Fragoso/NBAE/Getty ImagesWNBAWNBA star Brink launches withering attack on Kanter Freedom over anti-trans stuntLA star brands stunts as attempts to ‘stay relevant’Brink defends trans community in face of attacksOpinion: Kanter is using his freedom to punch downGuardian sportThu 27 Aug 2026 13.32 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 13.33 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLos Angeles Sparks star Cameron Brink has called former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom a “stupid piece of shit” who is “trying to stay relevant”, in the most vocal statement by an active player about Kanter Freedom’s recent actions involving the WNBA.Brink, the No 2 overall pick in the 2024 draft, spoke this week tothe Mirrorabout the controversies that have surrounded the league this summer.After Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham told ESPN last month that transgender women should not be able to participate in women’s sports, the league became a battleground for national debate. The stir arose despite the fact that no player assigned male at birth has ever been on aWNBAroster. The league’s collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women but contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.Chicago Sky ban Enes Kanter Freedom from home games, calling him ‘a potential threat’Read moreFreedom, an 11-year NBA veteran who last played in 2022, and Royce White, another former NBA player, have publicly declared for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. League sources have said the two are not eligible and have framed their actions as publicity stunts.“For me, personally, I think when it comes to the trans issues that I believe you’re talking about, I think it’s a non-issue, and I think it’s people trying to just come for the trans community. I just don’t stand for that,” Brink said. “I don’t even know what the fuck his name is, Enes Kanter, he’s a stupid piece of shit and I think a lot of people think that. I think he’s just trying to stay relevant.“I think people are tuned in for the right reasons, and it’s great that we can all talk about things that are important and hard and you can have your opinions on that. But I think taking something that’s a non-issue right now and trying to use it for clickbait, for views, for likes, and then targeting a vulnerable community is just really low.”The Chicago SkybannedFreedom from their home games and deemed him a “potential threat” after he was involved in a confrontation with guard Natasha Cloud during a game last week andejectedfrom the arena. Freedom was sitting along the baseline wearing a black shirt that read “WOMAN noun. adult human female.” Cloud did not speak to media after the incident.“It was pretty clear to us that his purpose of coming here was trying to be provocative and just see how much attention he could get and stir up and create,” Sky team president Michael Alter later told reporters.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBrink won a national championship at Stanford before entering the WNBA in 2021. She is averaging 9.4 points and 5.0 rebounds for Los Angeles this season.Earlier this month, the WNBA issued a statementcriticizingthose trying to create a narrative about the participation of transgender women in sports. Commissioner Cathy Engelberthas denouncedpeople she said are trying to “sow divisiveness” and turn the league into a “political football”.Explore more on these topicsWNBALos Angeles SparksBasketballChicago SkynewsShareReuse this content

title: Champions League draw: Arsenal face Real Madrid, Man City get Barcelona and PSG | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Arsenal will host Real Madrid and visit Bayern Munich, Aston Villa entertain PSG and Liverpool face Inter at San Siro
Author: Nick Ames
Headline: Arsenal will host Real Madrid and visit Bayern Munich, Aston Villa entertain PSG and Liverpool face Inter at San Siro
Content: The Champions League draw takes place in Monte Carlo, with Thierry Henry and David Villa among in attendance.Photograph: Manon Cruz/ReutersView image in fullscreenThe Champions League draw takes place in Monte Carlo, with Thierry Henry and David Villa among in attendance.Photograph: Manon Cruz/ReutersChampions LeagueChampions League draw: Arsenal face Real Madrid, Man City get Barcelona and PSGManchester United will host Bayern MunichAston Villa welcome PSG; Liverpool go to InterNick Amesin Monte CarloThu 27 Aug 2026 13.44 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 17.49 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleArsenal face mouthwatering assignments against Real Madrid and Bayern Munich as they bid to go one better than last season’s agonising near miss and win a firstChampions Leaguetitle.Mikel Arteta’s side werepipped on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain in the final three months agoand will be expected to cruise through this season’s league phase. The bulk of their draw appears kind but they are tasked with a visit to the Allianz Arena to play Bayern, whom theybeat 3-1 at the Emirates Stadium last November, and host Real, who are once again under the charge of José Mourinho. Two seasons ago, Arsenalbeat the Spanish giants 3-0 at home in a quarter-final first leg, Declan Rice scoring two memorable free-kicks.Champions League 2026-27 league phase draw: Arsenal to play Real Madrid, Manchester City face PSG and Barça – as it happenedRead moreArsenal will also welcome Borussia Dortmund, Lille and the Azerbaijani debutants Sabah to north London. Their other away fixtures involve trips to Napoli, Slavia Prague and a reunion with their ex-player Héctor Bellerin at Real Betis.Manchester City will swiftly renew acquaintances with Rodri when they visit Barcelona during Enzo Maresca’s first Champions League campaign in charge. They will greet Kevin De Bruyne and Napoli at the Etihad Stadium, just as they did last season incruising to a 2-0 win. Their other home ties bring an enticing meeting with the reigning champions, PSG, a tie against Sporting and a visit by AEK Athens. Trips to Porto, RB Leipzig and Lens will round off their schedule.The return ofManchester Unitedto Europe’s elite competition throws up home games with Bayern, Roma, RB Leipzig and Sabah. Michael Carrick’s team will travel to Como, who are managed by Cesc Fàbregas, along with Atlético Madrid, Sporting and Villarreal.Liverpool will host Atlético, Porto, Villarreal and Lens. They visit Lask, the newcomers whosensationally beat Celtic on Tuesday, along with Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Inter in a relatively kind-looking set of games.Aston Villa, ravaged in recent weeks by the departures of key players, will hope to have strengthened sufficiently for a home tie with PSG and a visit to Barcelona. They will be heartened by astirring performance in their recent Super Cup defeat to Luis Enrique’s side in Salzburg. Borussia Dortmund, Fenerbahce and the Norwegian new boys Viking Stavanger will also visit Villa Park. Unai Emery will also take his team to Club Brugge, Galatasaray and Slavia Prague.Quick GuidePremier League teams' UCL opponentsShowManchester City:PSG (home), Barcelona (away), Sporting (h), Porto (a), Napoli (h), Leipzig (a), AEK Athens (h), Lens (a).Liverpool:Atlético Madrid (h), Inter (a), Porto (h), Club Brugge (a), Villarreal (h), Fenerbahce (a), Lens (h), Lask (a).Arsenal: Real Madrid (h), Bayern Munich (a), Borussia Dortmund (h), Real Betis (a), Lille (h), Napoli (a), Sabah (h), Slavia Prague (a).Aston Villa: PSG (h), Barcelona (a), Dortmund (h), Club Brugge (a), Fenerbahce (h), Galatasaray (a), Viking (h), Slavia Prague (a).Manchester United:Bayern (h), Atletico (a), Roma (h), Sporting (a), Leipzig (h), Villarreal (a), Sabah (h), Como (a).Order of fixtures to be confirmed by UefaWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.While Chelsea did not qualify for European competition this season, their home will still host Champions League football. The Ukrainian champions, Shakhtar Donetsk, still unable to play continental matches in their homeland, will stage home games there. Real Madrid are the most high-profile of their four visitors, meaning Mourinho will return to his old stomping ground.PSG’s bid to win a third successive Champions League title involves home league games against Barcelona, Roma, Galatasaray and Slovan Bratislava, as well as trips to Villarreal, Como, City and Villa.The first set of fixtures will be played on 8 and 9 September. The schedule and dates for all eight match weeks will be announced on Saturday.Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueArsenalManchester CityManchester UnitedLiverpoolAston VillanewsShareReuse this content

title: Uefa raises stakes with criminal complaint in battle to unseat Infantino | Uefa | The Guardian
description: Uefa has begun a legal process against the embattled Fifa president but it will still be an uphill struggle to remove him
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Uefa has begun a legal process against the embattled Fifa president but it will still be an uphill struggle to remove him
Content: The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, with his Uefa counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in 2021. The two organisations are locked in a war of words over Fifa’s abandoned FFE proposal.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAView image in fullscreenThe Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, with his Uefa counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in 2021. The two organisations are locked in a war of words over Fifa’s abandoned FFE proposal.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAUefaAnalysisUefa raises stakes with criminal complaint in battle to unseat InfantinoMatt HughesUefa has begun a legal process against the embattled Fifa president but it will still be an uphill struggle to remove himThu 27 Aug 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 16.58 EDTShareAnyone who interpreted Uefa’s decision to withdraw a proposed boycott of Fifa competitions,revealed by the Guardian on Wednesday, as a backward step in the attempt to remove Gianni Infantino as Fifa’s president has been quickly disabused of that notion.In a stunning development that overshadowed one of the biggest days in the European football calendar as national football federation and club executives gathered for the Champions League draw in Monte Carlo, Uefa announced it waspreparing to make a legal complaintagainst Infantino in Switzerland alleging “criminal mismanagement” for his role in the failed World Cup sell-off plan.Uefa, having removed the immediate pressure on Fifa on one front bypermitting European teams to playin next month’s Under-20 Women’s World Cup and October’s senior Women’s World Cup qualifiers, has dramatically increased the stakes on another.The first step in that legal process is seeking disclosure in the United States of documents relating to the abandonedFifaForward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which Uefa described in a 56-page document sent to three US courts as having an “absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20bn” (£14.7bn).From the moment it became clear Infantino would not resign after withdrawing the FFE plan four days after it became public,Uefahas been pursuing the valuation issue, which if the sale had progressed would have enabled Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital to buy 21% of future Fifa revenues in perpetuity for $4.2bn.The Guardian revealed on 6 August that Uefa was commissioning an independent valuation of FFE amid concerns Infantino was planning to sell off football’s crown jewel on the cheap, a feeling exacerbated by the fact Fifa’s sales deck did not contain any information on the valuation process or evidence of a competitive tender.As one source who questioned Fifa’s valuation said this month: “We need to find out if they were selling the World Cup at a knockdown price.” The intention to bring a criminal complaint is the logical extension of this process.View image in fullscreenThe four-year cycle leading to this summer’s World Cup yielded $15bn in revenue for Fifa.Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPAEven the most cursory of inquiries over the past few weeks vindicated Uefa’s concerns. Fifa’s revenue for the four-year cycle that culminated in this summer’s World Cup was $15bn, leading market analysts to suggest that $20bn was a low valuation, particularly as the proposal did not appear to include provisions to prevent expansion and the creation of new tournaments.Kushner’s subsequent purchase of the LA Lakers with the former Disney chief Bob Iger for $12.5bn further convinced Uefa that Thrive Capital had been given a sweetheart deal by Infantino, a conviction underlined by its suspicion that Infantino was lining up a lucrative role worth tens of millions of pounds a year as FFE’s chair after standing down as Fifa’s president, which he plans to do in 2031 if he wins a further, final term.Infantino’s determination to cling to office – demonstrated by his decision to enter campaign mode byattending a meeting of the Caribbean Football Unionlast weekend in the Dominican Republic where, as the Guardian revealed, he suddenly approved several funding projects – emboldened Uefa further.Uefa has taken the legal route after being thwarted in numerous requests to Fifa to disclose documents. It has made court filings in New York, Florida and Colorado to obtain papers it may submit to Swiss courts seeking criminal charges.Just as significant as the attempt to take Infantino to court in his adopted country is Uefa’s attempt to rally Fifa members behind it in its attempt to unseat him via March’s presidential election.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFor all Uefa’s public bullishness that Infantino’s race is run, several senior figures there and among its allies at Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – have admitted concerns to the Guardian that they are struggling to get many member associations outside Europe to turn against him.Over the past few weeks several FAs have privately indicated it may take evidence of criminal activity, or at least proof that Infantino would have been personally enriched by the FFE venture, for them to abandon him.Even those with a brief knowledge of Fifa’s history would agree that the rebels concerned about momentum to unseat Infantino stalling have a point. Although he loves to paint the world governing body as the ultimate democracy underpinned by a one-member, one-vote system, the reality is anything but. Although elections are held every four years there have been only three permanent presidents in the past 52 years, and the last to leave office after a vote was England’s Sir Stanley Rous in 1974.Rous’s conqueror, the Brazilian João Havelange, resigned after 24 years and was later found to have accepted bribes related to the sale of media rights by a Fifa ethics committee. His successor, Sepp Blatter, stood down after winning five elections in the midst of an FBI investigation in 2015, which has resulted in more than 20 criminal convictions in the US and could lead to more.Any hope among the rebels that the Swiss authorities will come to their aid and bring Infantino to court should be tempered by those authorities’ long history of turning a blind eye to Fifa corruption, which meant intervention from the FBI was required to expose and punish it.Explore more on these topicsUefaFifaGianni InfantinoFootball politicsanalysisShareReuse this content

title: USA’s Russell and Brazil’s Dos Santos smash world records on ‘crazy’ night in Zurich | Athletics | The Guardian
description: Masai Russell and Alison Dos Santos broke world records as Mondo Duplantis prevailed in a historic pole vault duel on a remarkable night in Zurich
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Masai Russell and Alison Dos Santos broke world records as Mondo Duplantis prevailed in a historic pole vault duel on a remarkable night in Zurich
Content: Masai Russell celebrates after winning the women’s 100m hurdles in a world-record 12.09sec at the Diamond League meeting in Zurich.Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPAView image in fullscreenMasai Russell celebrates after winning the women’s 100m hurdles in a world-record 12.09sec at the Diamond League meeting in Zurich.Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPAAthleticsUSA’s Russell and Brazil’s Dos Santos smash world records on ‘crazy’ night in ZurichDos Santos and Russell smash hurdles world recordsWerro comes within 0.42sec of 800m world recordBednarek and Wanyonyi clock world-leading timesAgenciesThu 27 Aug 2026 17.05 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 17.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMasai Russell and Alison Dos Santos each set a world record while Mondo Duplantis won a historic pole vault on a frenetic Thursday night in Zurich.The Letzigrund Stadium had a raucous sell-out 25,000 crowd and the still, balmy weather conditions helped the athletes no end.Brazil’s Dos Santos was the first to make a mark, clocking a sensational 45.80 seconds in the 400m hurdlesto beat the previous mark of 45.94secset by Norway’s Karsten Warholm in the final of the Tokyo Olympics.“I have been showing great form throughout the season – that I am fast, I am strong,” said Dos Santos, with Warholm finishing second and dubbing their discipline a “crazy event”.“As soon as I knew I was coming here, I was excited. The weather’s good, the track’s amazing,” the Brazilian added.Then came US star Russell, the Olympic champion, timing 12.09sec in the 100m hurdlesto beat the previous best of 12.12secset by Nigeria’s Tobi Amusan at the Eugene world championships in 2022.Allow Instagram content?This article includes content provided byInstagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueDos Santos and Russell will leave Zurich with a cheque each for $80,000 for having broken their respective records.The world records were punctuated by a scintillating competition in the pole vault, eventually won by double Olympic and triple world champion Duplantis. The US-born Swede came under real pressure from Greek rival Emmanouil Karalis, who vaulted a personal best of 6.20m. Duplantis cleared 6.25m for victory, while both vaulters tried a possible world record 6.32m, in a truly thrilling showdown that gripped the stadium’s attention.It was the first time in vaulting history that two athletes had gone beyond the 6.20m mark.“It’s not every day two people go for the world record, so that was nuts,” said Karalis.The icing on the cake came in the women’s 800m, with the star attraction Switzerland’s own Audrey Werro. Werro also did not disappoint, registering the third fastest time ever in the two-lap race, 1:53.70, as she edged ever closer to Jarmila Kratochvilova’s Cold War world record of 1:53.28 set in Munich in 1983.“It was crazy, I am very proud. Thank you everybody!” the 22-year-old said.Femke Broeders-Bol finished second as she continues to improve in her transition from the 400m hurdles in which she was twice a world champion.“Being in a great event with a great time – amazing,” the Dutch athlete said.View image in fullscreenA fan holds a sign urging Armand Duplantis towards a world record as the Swede attempts 6.32m after winning the men’s pole vault at the Diamond League meeting in Zurich.Photograph: Fabrice Coffrini/AFP/Getty ImagesKenya’s world and Olympic champion Emmanuel Wanyonyi held off Algeria’s Djamel Sedjati for a nail-biting victory in the men’s 800m.Wanyonyi has said that going for David Rudisha’s world record of 1:40.91 is like running a marathon under two hours, and the mark once again proved elusive as he timed a world lead of 1:41.76 for the win. Sedjati was just 0.07sec adrift.“When I see the world records being broken, I know my time will come. There is time for everything,” said Wanyonyi.Explore more on these topicsAthleticsUSA Olympic teamUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Is NBC’s Premier League coverage in the US too English? | Premier League | The Guardian
description: One wonders when, if ever, a US broadcast can win the same plaudits presenting the English league with a more American voice
Author: Leander Schaerlaeckens
Headline: One wonders when, if ever, a US broadcast can win the same plaudits presenting the English league with a more American voice
Content: The new Premier League season kicked off last week.Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe new Premier League season kicked off last week.Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueIs NBC’s Premier League coverage in the US too English?Leander SchaerlaeckensOne wonders when, if ever, a US broadcast can win the same plaudits presenting the English league with a more American voiceThu 27 Aug 2026 12.36 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 13.47 EDTShareThere they were again, signaling with their unchanging faces and voices and their unchanging studio backdrop that anotherPremier Leagueseason had begun. On Friday afternoon, and again on Saturday and Sunday morning, Rebecca Lowe welcomed American viewers to what is somehow already the 14th season of the world’s most popular sporting circuit to air on NBC.She was flanked, as ever, by her merry band of pundits, her gang of fellow British expats. The Robbies and the other ones. Also, Tim Howard as the token American, albeit one who spent 13 seasons of his goalkeeping career in the Premier League, deemed sufficiently English by osmosis to join the crew.Post-Pep Premier League era begins with blast of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney RonayRead moreThe games’ announcers would be British, too. And they would all speak of “football” and “pitches” and “away matches.” Teams would be “they,” of course. The ads, too, would sound very English, supremely English, maximally English. For Barclays, among other longtime sponsors leaning hard into the image of the beleaguered American fan, embattled but persevering in his or her niche pursuit of following this plucky little league that airs on one of the nation’s most readily available channels.Taking it all in, I couldn’t help but think back to watching the BBC’s coverage of the final day of the last season for the first time in years with some English expat friends and some VPN trickery. It struck me that somehow, despite originating from the country, it didn’t actually look or sound or feel quite as English-coded as theNBCoffering of the events. Except for the diversity of mellifluous regional accents on offer on the BBC, NBC has out-Englished the English.Other broadcasters have chosen different approaches. Fox leans into its Americanness as hard as NBC does the Englishness in its World Cup presentation. Apple sits somewhere in the middle, on neutral ground, when it airs Major League Soccer.If Major League Baseball’s core product is really nostalgia, and the NFL’s is consumerism and nationalism, then the Premier League’s, going by NBC’s presentation, is anglophilia. It’s all there. The satellite zoom-ins on the league’s quaint stadiums nestled between the brick row houses. The reverence for the club anthems and traditions. The poppies pinned to the on-air talent’s lapels every November to commemorate Britain’s fallen soldiers – a tradition which doesn’t entirely resonate in an American context.NBC’s unsaid sales pitch feels like it should be: Catch a match, and you, too, could look and sound and feel more English, to yourself and to all your friends.For NBC’s part, this has been a perfectly justifiable and coherent business strategy. And it has worked outstandingly well for the broadcaster. In a landscape of shrinking audiences, NBC’s Premier League viewers seem to tick up every year andposted their highest totals ever last season.And in a way, all of this is baked into the recipe. Soccer owes much of its rise in these United States to the worldliness it confers. As the upper middle class discovered soccer – or rediscovered it, to be historically accurate – in the late 1990s and early 2000s, following it signaled that you knew there was more to sports than the NFL, NBA or baseball. That the rest of world mostly followed different sports, and that you were in on its secrets. Bonus points for drinking a Carling in a pub of some American downtown at 7.30 am on a Saturday.But the question that is now imposing itself is how and when the US will develop its own soccer culture, where it no longer has to apologize for its quirks and its lingo. The wildly profitable –almost counterproductively profitable– 2026 World Cup demonstrated anew that the US has been a soccer country for a long time. The sport is mature here now. It is long past needing to establish itself and is now on to the trickier work of consolidating its status and making the smaller gains.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionYet American soccer remains beset by a sense that it doesn’t entirely belong. Its players and teams must still scrap to be taken seriously outside their own borders. There is an unmistakable undercurrent of imposter syndrome running through our soccer scene. And when the sport’s most popular games are presented with an English accent, it stunts the growth of something authentic. How can an organic soccer culture blossom here, after belatedly taking root in the supporter sections of the many MLS and NWSL teams that rushed to brand themselves as “football club”, when NBC’s coverage chooses to stand in the shadow of another?This isn’t to diminish NBC’s Premier League crew or their otherwise excellent work or indeed their career choices. And part of the appeal of the US is that, at its best, it accepts the cultures and norms of the world and finds a place to integrate those things into a kaleidoscopic whole.Lowe even announced that she was a naturalized citizen in 2022.But eventually, American soccer will have to start doing its own things in its own way, rather than just copying what the cool soccer countries are doing. And, among other tasks, that means acknowledging that we speak differently. One wonders what that could do for the growth of the game here.Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: U.S. Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts,which is out now. He teaches at Marist University.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueUS sports mediaNBCNBC UniversalUS television industrycommentShareReuse this content

title: Callaway cuts ties with Good Good Golf over ad depicting violence against woman | Golf | The Guardian
description: Callaway has endeed its relationship with Good Good Golf and pledged $1m to domestic violence groups after backlash over controversial advertisement
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Callaway has endeed its relationship with Good Good Golf and pledged $1m to domestic violence groups after backlash over controversial advertisement
Content: Good Good Golf co-founder Garrett Clark has apologized amid mounting fallout over a since-deleted advertisement that was criticized for depicting violence against women.Photograph: Ben Jared/PGA TOURView image in fullscreenGood Good Golf co-founder Garrett Clark has apologized amid mounting fallout over a since-deleted advertisement that was criticized for depicting violence against women.Photograph: Ben Jared/PGA TOURGolfCallaway cuts ties with Good Good Golf over ad depicting violence against womanGolf giant ends partnership with YouTube groupRetailers have pulled Good Good products from shelvesGarrett Clark says controversial skit was in ‘poor taste’Guardian sportand agenciesThu 27 Aug 2026 16.15 EDTFirst published on Thu 27 Aug 2026 15.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCallaway has ended its relationship with Good GoodGolfamid mounting fallout from an advert that many believe made light of violence against women.The golf equipment manufacturer announced the decision on Thursday, cutting ties with one of the world’s most popular YouTube sports channels effective immediately. Callaway also said it would donate $1m to organizations working to prevent violence against women and support survivors of domestic violence.Good Good Golf co-founder Garrett Clark apologized in a video on Wednesday night, saying he hopes “we can move on” amid continued fallout from an advert that many believe made light of violence against women.LIV Golf to lay off majority of staff amid ‘compressed timeline’ for new investorsRead moreThe video, ⁠posted on 21 August, was meant to promote a driver it had produced alongside Callaway. Itshowed Clark shovingGood Good personality Alexis Miestowski to the ground as she went to pull the Callaway club out of his bag. Clark then said, “Do not touch my new driver,” while ⁠standing over her.Good Good is one of the world’s most popular YouTube sports channels and has been credited with bringing golf to a younger audience.The ad drew ⁠immediate backlash with claims ​it depicted violence against women, and Good Good quickly removed it from social media. The company issued an apology on Saturday, and Clark added a personal apology in a video posted to his social media Wednesday night.Callaway, which had reposted the ad to its own social media accounts, acknowledged on Thursday that its internal review process had not been comprehensive enough and said it had taken “appropriate internal corrective actions” and strengthened its approval process.“Over the past several days, we have listened and reflected deeply on the hurt and disappointment caused by the video we reposted,” Callaway said in a statement. “We heard from individuals who shared personal experiences related to violence against women, and their stories were powerful reminders that this issue touches the lives of far too many people.“Unequivocally, violence against women is unacceptable and should never be trivialized, normalized, or used as entertainment.”Clark also apologized. “I personally want ⁠to apologize for playing a role in the skit, in this ad, at the magnitude that I did,” Clark said. “And then on Good Good’s behalf and on Good Good marketing team’s behalf, I wanted to say an apology as well ⁠because this is not at all what we stand for, the way that this ad was received is not how Good Good is, and it’s not ​what we stand for, once again.“I want everyone to know that ‌I do not support [domestic violence] abuse or any ‌of that of any kind.“The fallout from the ad has been swift and could continue to reverberate throughout the golf industry.Golf Channel postponed the ‌premiere of the reality show Big Break x Good Good by a week after a sponsor requested that its branding be removed. Dick’s Sporting Goods and Golf Galaxy are among the retailers to have pulled Good Good merchandise from their in-store shelves and online.Good Good is also the title sponsor of aPGA Tourevent scheduled for November in Austin, Texas. Tour commissioner Brian Rolapp was asked ahead of this week’s Tour Championship whether the controversy could affect that sponsorship.“It’s a bit of a fluid situation,” he said. “We’ll continue to monitor the situation and see how it develops.”In his Wednesday video of more than eight minutes, Clark outlined how the ad was ​produced, sharing behind-the-scenes footage showing that ‌he did not strike Miestowski, who played golf at Indiana University ​and contributes to Good Good’s women-focused YouTube channel.Clark added that he was “cringing” once he saw the ad, and condemned those who have sent negative messages to Miestowski on social media.“Good Good messed up by promoting a very poor-taste ad, but hopefully you guys can forgive Good Good as well as myself for being a part of it,” Clark said. “Hopefully we can move on and grow the women’s side of golf, because that is one of our huge, huge ‌goals.”Explore more on these topicsGolfPGA TourUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Struggling Inter Miami hire Kily González as new head coach | MLS | The Guardian
description: Lionel Messi and Co are currently mired in a five-match winless run overseen by interim head coach Guillermo Hoyos
Author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer
Headline: Lionel Messi and Co are currently mired in a five-match winless run overseen by interim head coach Guillermo Hoyos
Content: Kily González has managed three clubs since retiring as a player, all in Argentina.Photograph: Luciano Bisbal/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenKily González has managed three clubs since retiring as a player, all in Argentina.Photograph: Luciano Bisbal/Getty ImagesMLSStruggling Inter Miami hire Kily González as new head coachMLS club mired in five-match winless runGonzález to replace interim coach Guillermo HoyosPablo Iglesias MaurerandGuardian sportThu 27 Aug 2026 17.04 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 18.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleInter Miami have hired former Argentina international Cristian “Kily” González as the club’s new head coach, according to two sources familiar with negotiations. César Luis Merlo was first to report the news.The hiring will spell the end of interim manager Guillermo Hoyos’ time in charge of the South Florida club. In fact, he may have already coached his last game;MLSannounced on Thursday that Hoyos had been suspended for one game for the club’s “repeated violations” of the late kickoff policy. (Inter Miami have become known throughout the league for delaying their return from half-time.)Hoyos took over after head coach Javier Mascherano resigned for personal reasons on 14 April, several weeks after the club crashed out of the Concacaf Champions Cup on aggregate to Nashville SC in the last 16. Hoyos was previously an assistant coach with the club after being initially hired as the head of methodology for the club’s academy. It is not yet known if he will remain with the club after his stint as interim manager.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDouble-elimination, reseeding and 20 teams: MLS plans potential overhaul of playoffsRead moreInter Miami have been in bad form since returning from MLS’s World Cup break, winning three times in nine games, with the most recent victory coming on 5 August in the Leagues Cup against Atlético San Luis. The Herons were eliminated from that competition in the group stage on 12 August with a 3-2 loss to León, which was followed by a 4-1 drubbing in MLS league play at the hands of Nashville SC. They are now riding a five-match winless run, with the final four of those results coming with Lionel Messi on the field, havingreturned after the death of his father, Jorge.Hoyos has a long history with Messi. He is credited by some with discovering the player as coach of a Barcelona youth squad in the early 2000s. González does not have nearly the same level of direct history with Messi, but he does hail from Rosario, Messi’s home town. Their playing careers overlapped, but only barely: the final two of González’s 56 appearances with Argentina came in World Cup 2006 qualifiers against Uruguay and Peru in 2005; Messi also played in those games, earning his third and fourth caps. The two only shared the field in the first game against Peru; against Uruguay, Messi came on as a sub for González in the second half.Since moving into management, González has taken charge of Argentine clubs Rosario Central from 2020 to 2022, Unión from 2023 to 2025 and most recently Platense for 14 games last year. He has lost more games than he has won at every stop, and owns a career win percentage of 32.5%.Inter Miami currently trail Nashville by 10 points in the Eastern Conference standings, sitting third in the Supporters’ Shield table behind the Tennessee side and the Western Conference-leading Vancouver Whitecaps. The clubwon MLS Cuplast season and were favorites to defend their title this year, particularly after adding wide defender Sergio Reguilón, 2025 MLS goalkeeper of the year Dayne St Clair, Monterrey striker Germán Berterame and the post-World Cup addition of Brazilian midfielder Casemiro.Explore more on these topicsMLSInter MiamiLionel MessiUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: US Open: Carlos Alcaraz to face Safiullin on return as Sabalenka gets tricky draw | US Open Tennis 2026 | The Guardian
description: Carlos Alcaraz faces the in-form Russian Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open while Aryna Sabalenka will take on Camila Osorio at Flushing Meadows
Author: Tumaini Carayol
Headline: Carlos Alcaraz faces the in-form Russian Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open while Aryna Sabalenka will take on Camila Osorio at Flushing Meadows
Content: Carlos Alcaraz returns to competitive singles action for the first time in fourth months to defend his US Open crown.Photograph: Marcin Cholewinski/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenCarlos Alcaraz returns to competitive singles action for the first time in fourth months to defend his US Open crown.Photograph: Marcin Cholewinski/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockUS Open Tennis 2026US Open: Carlos Alcaraz to face Safiullin on return as Sabalenka gets tricky drawAlcaraz back in action after four-month injury layoffNovak Djokovic faces Mariano Navone in first roundTumaini Carayolin New YorkThu 27 Aug 2026 14.34 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 16.17 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCarlos Alcaraz has been handed a tough draw on his return to singles competition after a four-month injury layoff as he faces the in-form Russian Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open.‘Grand slams are the engine to make a living’: Mackenzie McDonald on why players still compete when injuredRead moreAlcaraz, the defending champion in New York, has not competed in singles since sustaining a right wrist injury at the Barcelona Open in April, with the Spaniard missing the French Open, where he was also the defending champion, and Wimbledon. He was understandably rusty and tentative with his first serve when making his first competitive appearance since the injuryalongside Serena Williams in the mixed doubles eventon Tuesday, with the pair losing in the quarter-finals and the 44-year-old Williams even outperforming him during large parts of their time on court. His opening match against the world No 98 Safiullin, who has risen more than 100 places in the world rankings this year after returning from injury and defeated Alcaraz indoors at the Paris Masters in 2023, will be a significant first challenge.Between the uncertainty surrounding Alcaraz due to his lack of match play and the absence of the world No 1, Jannik Sinner,who was forced to withdraw due to a knee injury, the men’s Flushing Meadows draw is as open as it has been in years. As the second seed, Alcaraz’s section includes both the eighth seed, Ben Shelton, and the 10th seed, Arthur Fils, the winners of the Canadian Openand Cincinnati Openrespectively, the two ATP Masters 1000 events leading up to the US Open. Fils will face a high-profile first-round opponent in the former world No 3, Stefanos Tsitsipas.The four-time champion Novak Djokovic will begin his latest attempt to become the oldest singles grand slam champion in the open era as the fourth seed in Alcaraz’s half of the draw. He faces Mariano Navone in the first round with the out-of-form seventh seed Daniil Medvedev the highest-ranked seed in the Serb’s quarter. Alexander Zverev, the French Open champion, is the top seed at a grand slam tournament for the first time and faces the Italian Lorenzo Sonego in his opener.While a large group of players have an opportunity to make a career-defining breakthrough in the men’s draw, it will be difficult for the rank-and-file competitors to stop the strong group of elite players at the top of the women’s draw despite their differing form. Aryna Sabalenka, the defending champion, will begin against Camila Osorio as she tries to hold on to her No 1 ranking after a difficult few months.View image in fullscreenAryna Sabalenka (left) and Jessica Pegula may meet in the semi-finals, a potential rerun of the 2024 final that Sabalenka won.Photograph: Frank Franklin II/APThe highest ranked players in Sabalenka’s half are the in-form third seed, Jessica Pegula, a potential semi-final opponent, the Wimbledon champion and sixth seed, Linda Noskova, and the seventh seed, Karolina Muchova, the runner-up at Wimbledon. However, considering Sabalenka’s recent results, even a potential third-round match with the two-time grand slam champion and 27th seed, Barbora Krejcikova, cannot be taken for granted.The strong bottom half of the draw, meanwhile, is overflowing with title contenders.. Elena Rybakina, the second seed, seemed to be in an ideal position to usurp Sabalenka at the top of the rankings but her form is uncertain after she was forced to retire from her quarter-final against Iga Swiatek in Cincinnati last week due to a leg injury.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSwiatek, the eighth seed, and the fourth seed, Coco Gauff, were the two most notable performers in the buildup to the US Open, winning in Toronto and Cincinnati respectively. Swiatek could face Rybakina in the quarter-finals, while the highest ranked player in Coco Gauff’s section is the French Open champion and fifth seed, Mirra Andreeva. Other contenders include the 13th seed and two-time champion Naomi Osaka, who could face Rybakina in round four, and last year’s runner-up Amanda Anisimova.Explore more on these topicsUS Open Tennis 2026US Open tennisTennisnewsShareReuse this content

title: Danny Welbeck leads Chelsea past Luton but Enzo Fernández misses Carabao Cup tie | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Danny Welbeck scored his first goal for Chelsea in their 2-0 win over Luton in the Carabao Cup second round, but Enzo Fernández was left out
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Danny Welbeck scored his first goal for Chelsea in their 2-0 win over Luton in the Carabao Cup second round, but Enzo Fernández was left out
Content: Danny Welbeck heads Chelsea into the lead early in the second half.Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDanny Welbeck heads Chelsea into the lead early in the second half.Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesCarabao CupDanny Welbeck leads Chelsea past Luton but Enzo Fernández misses Carabao Cup tieJacob Steinbergat Stamford BridgeThu 27 Aug 2026 16.40 EDTLast modified on Fri 28 Aug 2026 00.24 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEmiliano Martínez is on his way but another high-profile Argentinian is likely to be wearing a different shade of blue soon.Chelseahave dealt with their biggest weakness, satisfying Xabi Alonso’s wish for a new goalkeeper by agreeing a £7.5m deal to sign Martínez from Aston Villa, and it will surely not be long before they have put an end to the Enzo Fernández saga.Fernández was the most notable absentee as Chelsea eased into the third round of theCarabao Cupwith a 2-0 win over Luton. There is a desire to move on from the circus. Manchester City are poised to bid for Fernández and, with the noise around the midfielder becoming a distraction, Alonso and the club decided to leave out Chelsea’s supposed vice-captain.‘I can’t wait’: Liam Delap seals £45m Nottingham Forest move from ChelseaRead moreAlonso explained that he had to think about the team. Chelsea’s manager was diplomatic. Alonso said that Fernández has been training well. He offered political answers but did not douse the sense that Fernández has played his last game for Chelsea, who host Leeds in the next round.It is for the best. Fernández has been looking for a way out since March and Chelsea need committed players. Alonso wants to improve the squad’s culture and the attitude against Luton was good. Danny Welbeck, still going strong at 35, can be a standard bearer after joining from Brighton. The striker is not here to make up the numbers and played a key role in this win, grabbing his first goal since joining when he opened the scoring early in the second half.“Danny was the patient player,” Alonso said of Welbeck breaking Luton’s resistance by leaping to head home a fine cross from Malo Gusto. “He did what he does best: score and to be in the right place.”Welbeck will provide competition for João Pedro in attack this season. He also adds a vital dash of experience to a young squad. Chelsea can cope without Fernández, even though they will need to replace him if he goes to City.View image in fullscreenXabi Alonso has seen his Chelsea side win their first two games.Photograph: Ian Stephen/Every Second Media/ShutterstockThe early vibes under Alonso are encouraging. He has been decisive with the goalkeeping position, as exemplified by his ruthless response to Robert Sánchez’s skittish display against Fulham. There is nothing left to see with Sánchez. He is not good enough and Chelsea had to be opportunistic when offered the chance to sign Martínez. Mike Penders made his debut in goal on Thursday night. The 21-year-old Belgian is highly rated but will be behind Martínez in the pecking order.Alonso is trying to win now. Although Chelsea have no European football this season it was surprising that they named such a strong side three days after their helter-skelter win over Fulham in the Premier League. Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer were part of an exciting attack and were supported by a thrilling display from Estêvão Willian on the right.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThird in League One, Luton battled to stay in contention during a first half in which the shot count was 17-3 in Chelsea’s favour. Rogers crashed an effort against the bar and Jack Wilshere’s side were defiant in defence. Josh Keeley made excellent saves from Palmer and Reece James, starting in midfield for the second time in three days despite his injury problems.Chelsea stayed patient. Valentin Barco, Jude Bellingham’s Atlanta irritant, had an impressive debut next to James. Chelsea, who were still missing Moisés Caicedo, upped the pace early in the second half. Gusto overlapped and crossed. Welbeck was wily and deadly, creeping off his marker and heading home.The second goal arrived late. Barco was involved and Palmer found Estêvão, whose shot went in off Hakeem Odoffin for an own goal.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupChelseaLuton Townmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Chelsea agree £7.5m deal to sign Emiliano Martínez from Aston Villa | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: Chelsea have agreed a deal for the Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez but Enzo Fernández has been left out of Thursday’s Carabao Cup tie
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Chelsea have agreed a deal for the Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez but Enzo Fernández has been left out of Thursday’s Carabao Cup tie
Content: Emiliano Martínez is out of favour at Aston Villa after the arrival of Zion Suzuki.Photograph: Agustín Marcarian/ReutersView image in fullscreenEmiliano Martínez is out of favour at Aston Villa after the arrival of Zion Suzuki.Photograph: Agustín Marcarian/ReutersChelseaChelsea agree £7.5m deal to sign Emiliano Martínez from Aston VillaEnzo Fernández left out of Luton Carabao Cup tieVilla sign Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka on freeJacob SteinbergThu 27 Aug 2026 14.19 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 18.49 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChelsea have agreed a £7.5m deal to sign the Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez and are expectingManchester Cityto make an offer for Enzo Fernández in the next 48 hours.Xabi Alonso identified the signing of a goalkeeper as a priority after Robert Sánchez struggled against Fulham on Monday and the deal for Martínez has gone through quickly. The Argentina international is out of favour at Villa after their acquisition of Zion Suzuki and is due to sign a two-year contract with the option of a further year.The signing of Martínez, who will be 34 next week, will raise questions over the future of Sánchez. Sources believe the Spaniard is unlikely to accept losing his spot as No 1 and may need to be moved on before the window shuts on Tuesday night.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.However iIt is unclear whether there is an obvious club for Sánchez to join and another complication forChelseawill be working out what to do with Mike Penders, who was expected to challenge for the No 1 shirt this season. There is a feeling that Penders could leave on loan. The highly rated 21-year-old Belgian spent last season on loan at Strasbourg.It is poised to be a busy end to the summer for Chelsea, who are also dealing with City’s attempts to sign Fernández. The Argentina midfielder is desperate to leave and was left out of the side for Thursday night’s Carabao Cup tie against Luton.Sources at Chelsea insist a deal is not close and that there has yet to be any communication from City. Chelsea are adamant that Fernández will be sold only on their terms.City missed an unofficial deadlineto sign the midfielder for £120m this month and there have been suggestions the price could be higher because the end of the window is approaching.Chelsea also need to be able to strengthen their squad but have little time to act. They are aware Bournemouth do not want to sell Alex Scott and that Crystal Palace are similarly determined to hold on to Adam Wharton, while Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara could be a target. Chelsea may not look for a direct replacement for Fernández, but will not accept weakening their squad by helping out a rival.View image in fullscreenLeon Goretzka has joined Aston Villa after leaving Bayern Munich earlier this summer.Photograph: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC/Getty ImagesAston Villa, meanwhile, have signed the Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free after his departure from Bayern Munich. The 31-year-old spent eight seasons at ​Bayern, making ‌312 appearances, and has played 73 times for his country.“I had a bit of long vacation, and it was a process to find out what I really wanted. From the first moment, I had a really good feeling, and I’m really happy to be here,” Goretzka said after completing the move.“I had a good feeling from the first conversation with the coach. Aston Villa is a really big club. I want to help the team to achieve their goals and to bring my experience that I have from my whole career.”“I’m really looking forward to playing in these kinds of big games every few days,” he added. “This is probably the biggest difference to the Bundesliga, where you have only several great games with big opponents.”Explore more on these topicsChelseaAston VillaTransfer windowManchester CitynewsShareReuse this content

title: Muniz and García on target in Fulham’s Carabao Cup cruise past Wimbledon | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Emile Smith Rowe opened the scoring as Fulham eased to a 3-0 win against AFC Wimbledon, setting up a third-round trip to West Ham
Author: John Brewin
Headline: Emile Smith Rowe opened the scoring as Fulham eased to a 3-0 win against AFC Wimbledon, setting up a third-round trip to West Ham
Content: Rodrigo Muniz points to the sky after scoring Fulham’s second goal.Photograph: Tom Dulat/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRodrigo Muniz points to the sky after scoring Fulham’s second goal.Photograph: Tom Dulat/Getty ImagesCarabao CupMuniz and García on target in Fulham’s Carabao Cup cruise past WimbledonJohn Brewinat Craven CottageThu 27 Aug 2026 17.01 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 18.58 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFulham’s second London derby this week, a first competitive win for Álvaro Arbeloa. IfAFC Wimbledonrepresent a different echelon to Chelsea, Monday’s visitors, Thursday’s easy progress past League One opponents supplied several reasons for optimism in the new Fulham.Marco Silva, Arbeloa’s predecessor, frequently offered sullen dismissal of the depth of hisFulhamsquad and yet left behind plenty of talent on departing for Benfica.
