Getting a better tune from Emile Smith Rowe and Rodrigo Muniz than Silva managed last season will help. The pair scored first-half goals to take the tie from Wimbledon’s reach, making for a second half of comfort and experimentation, glimpses of a different Fulham, teenage talent handed its chance to shine. Gonzalo García’s late strike, rounding Wimbledon goalkeeper Nathan Bishop for a second goal of the week, increased the excitement surrounding one of the summer’s most eye-catching signings.Danny Welbeck leads Chelsea past Luton as Fernández misses Carabao Cup tieRead more“You need the energy and different qualities,” said Arbeloa of an evening where squad rotation had paid dividends. “They need to feel they are important.”A muggy riverside evening attracted a decent crowd. More than enough to disrupt the dog walkers and evening strollers of a genteel locale, the Wimbledon contingent boisterous. The first meeting between the clubs since 2001, before the old Wimbledon was franchised to Milton Keynes and a phoenix club rose from that rotten affair.The respective team selections revealed priorities; 10 changes for Arbeloa, only Oscar Bobb remained from Chelsea; six for Johnnie Jackson, the Wimbledon manager. Shea Charles, the summer’s other headline signing, made his first start and played well. “He’s ready,” said Arbeloa of the young Northern Ireland midfielder.Luc De Fougerolles, fresh from the summer’s World Cup with Canada, made only his second Fulham appearance. Down each team’s left, a Sessegnon brother, Ryan for Fulham and Steven, formerly of Fulham, for Wimbledon.“A good night for the club because we get to test ourselves against the very best,” said Jackson. “And 5,000 fans got to enjoy themselves. They were a credit to the club.”Wimbledon, maintaining Crazy Gang traditions, were dangerous from set pieces. When De Fougerolles could only head away a corner, the ball fell to the Wimbledon captain, Alistair Smith. The shot was straight at Benjamin Lecomte, the best chance on offer to the visitors all evening.Thereafter, Fulham piled up opportunities. Goals soon followed. Smith Rowe was furious after a sliced miss. Muniz was just as self-flagellating when ballooning a Smith Rowe flick.View image in fullscreenGonzalo García completes Fulham’s 3-0 victory to set up a London derby with West Ham.Photograph: Dennis Goodwin/ProSports/ShutterstockHis redemption came swiftly, from close range after Dons defender James Tilley deflected the ball into his path. The celebration was minimal from a player Arbeloa said “deserves more minutes”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMuniz was far more rapturous after nodding in Kenny Tete’s cross. Small wonder. This was his first goal since the opening game of last season. “Goals are very important for strikers,” said Arbeloa, stating the clear and obvious.At half-time Macaulay Zepa, 18, arrived. Arbeloa’s appointment was accompanied by heralding of his youth development work at Real Madrid, a departure from Silva’s preference for hard-bitten pros. Zepa, a speedy and direct winger, showed real promise, as did fellow youth team graduate Chibby Nwoko. “One of the best news today,” said Arbeloa. “We know very well that academy players are very important.”Fulham featured an assured youth-and-experience central defensive combination of De Fougerolles and Joachim Andersen. Calvin Bassey replaced the senior partner on the hour and the youngster did not last much longer, pulling up after a block tackle. “Nothing to worry about,” said Arbeloa, soothingly.The arrivals of García and César Palacios, young Madrilenos who accompanied Arbeloa, supplied further excitement, the former’s goal another taste of a new Fulham.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupFulhamAFC Wimbledonmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Atlético Madrid chief insists Júlian Alvarez will ‘never, ever’ be sold to Barcelona | Atlético Madrid | The Guardian
description: Miguel Ángel Gil Marín has accused Barcelona of ‘dishonesty’ and appeared to close the door on the Argentina forward’s potential move
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Miguel Ángel Gil Marín has accused Barcelona of ‘dishonesty’ and appeared to close the door on the Argentina forward’s potential move
Content: Atlético Madrid have insisted they will ‘never, ever’ sell Júlian Alvarez to Barcelona.Photograph: Alberto Simon/DYDPPA/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenAtlético Madrid have insisted they will ‘never, ever’ sell Júlian Alvarez to Barcelona.Photograph: Alberto Simon/DYDPPA/ShutterstockAtlético MadridAtlético Madrid chief insists Júlian Alvarez will ‘never, ever’ be sold to BarcelonaMiguel Ángel Gil Marín accuses Barça of ‘dishonesty’Arsenal have also been linked with Argentina forwardReuters andGuardian sportThu 27 Aug 2026 18.16 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 18.17 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAtlético Madrid’s chief executive appeared to slam the door on Barcelona’s pursuit of Júlian Alvarez on Thursday. Miguel Ángel Gil Marín accused the Catalan club of dishonesty and insisted the Argentina forward would “never, ever” be sold to them.Speaking to Spanish broadcaster Movistar Plus, Gil Marín delivered a blistering response to ⁠Barcelona’s president, Joan Laporta, who had said on Wednesday that ​his club remained “very interested” in signing Alvarez.Julián Álvarez walks alone at Atlético in transfer saga with no end – and no winners | Sid LoweRead moreGil Marín said Atlético were united from top to bottom in refusing to negotiate with Barcelona over a deal for a player they insists is not for sale to theirLa Ligarivals.“The truth is that it outrages ⁠us even more; we are repulsed by the dishonesty, the lack of ethics, transparency and professionalism, and ​we can only insist that we will not ‌negotiate with Barcelona under any ‌circumstances,” Gil Marín said.“I have the support of everyone working with me, from shareholders to directors, and ‌the only certain and firm decision is that we will not negotiate with Barcelona under any circumstances,” he added. “You have my word – the player [Alvarez] will most certainly not be transferred to Barcelona.“The Barcelona vice-president, Rafa Yuste, reacted angrily to Gil Marín’s remarks. “It is a lack of manners and respect,” Yuste told Movistar. “With those words, they’ve crossed a red ‌line.”Earlier on Thursday, Atlético’s board of directors unanimously backed the club’s stance on Alvarez, ruling out talks with Barcelona and saying there was “zero consideration” of a transfer before the summer transfer window closes.Gil Marín said the situation had affected Alvarez. “Júlian is really struggling; there have been people who have set out to deceive and confuse him, and I’m very sorry about that,” Gil Marín said.Alvarez wasbooed by Atleti fansduring their 2-2 home draw with Villarreal on Sunday, having stated his desire to leave. While on World Cup duty with Argentina this summer, the 26-year-old revealed hewanted to “fulfil my dream”by departing the club.“I know him and we’ve been working with him for ⁠some time,” Gil Marín added. “He’s a great professional and footballer, but he’s very confused and going ​through a very difficult time, ​both personally and professionally.“Arsenalhave also been linkedwith a move for the former Manchester City forward, but Gil Marín said his preference was ​for the player to ‌remain in Madrid beyond Tuesday’s deadline.“Our intention ​and my personal dream ​is for him to stay with us, to remain at Atlético,” he said. “To compete amongst the greats, you need great players, and Júlian is one. If he believes that staying at Atlético is no longer feasible, we will look for an alternative, but it will never, ever be Barcelona.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionRodri makes Barça debut in win over AthleticRaphinha and Fermin López scored in either half and Rodri made his debut off the bench as Barcelona beat Athletic Club 2-0 at Camp Nou in their first home match of the new La Liga season.View image in fullscreenBarcelona midfielder Rodri applauds the Camp Nou crowd after making his debut.Photograph: Quique García/EPABarça opened the scoring in the 37th minute, Raphinga rounding goalkeeper Unai Simón after Pedri’s through ball split the Athletic defence. ⁠Fermin sealed the win ⁠in the 82nd ​when he pounced on Aymeric Laporte’s defensive error from Karim Adeyemi’s low cross and finished from inside the penalty box.Hansi Flick’s side controlled most of the ⁠game and created the better chances, although Simon kept the visitors in contention with several important saves. Flick also handed winger Anthony Gordon his full debut, with Rodri coming on for Raphinha to make his first appearance for Barça.Flick made three changes from the team that began the campaign ⁠with a 5-0 win at Elche, handing Anthony Gordon his full debut and bringing in Pau Cubarsi and ​Pedri. New signing Rodri started on the bench.“Happy to play my first match,” Rodri told Dazn after the game. “It is important for me to regain my rhythm and adapt to this great team. It has been a long summer … I’m very happy, I am where I wanted to be. Now we have to work.”Explore more on these topicsAtlético MadridTransfer windowBarcelonaLa LigaEuropean club footballnewsShareReuse this content

title: Rangers crash out of Conference League in shootout loss to Czech side Jablonec | Conference League | The Guardian
description: Derek McInnes’s side lost 4-3 on penalties to Jablonec after a 1-1 aggregate draw, while Brighton advanced with a second-leg rout of Tromsø
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Derek McInnes’s side lost 4-3 on penalties to Jablonec after a 1-1 aggregate draw, while Brighton advanced with a second-leg rout of Tromsø
Content: Rangers players react after Jablonec won their penalty shootout following a 1-1 draw on aggregate.Photograph: Milan Kammermayer/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenRangers players react after Jablonec won their penalty shootout following a 1-1 draw on aggregate.Photograph: Milan Kammermayer/ShutterstockConference LeagueRangers crash out of Conference League in shootout loss to Czech side JablonecMcInnes ‘mortified’ by early European exitBrighton rout Tromsø 4-0 to reach league phasePA MediaThu 27 Aug 2026 17.49 EDTFirst published on Thu 27 Aug 2026 16.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRangers crashed out of the UefaConference Leagueplayoffs with a 4-3 penalty shootout defeat by Jablonec.Leading 1-0 from the first leg at Ibrox last week, Derek McInnes’s side turned in a turgid performance in Czechia which lacked creativity and invention. It proved costly as they fell to a 1-0 defeat at Stadion Strelnice, drawing 1-1 on aggregate after extra time to set up the final shootout.Ten-man Hearts stun Rapid Vienna in shootout to reach Conference LeagueRead moreDespite McInnes introducing Lawrence Shankland, Connor Barron and Findlay Curtis in the second half,Rangerscould not get a foothold in the game. The Jablonec midfielder Vakhtang Chanturishvili deservedly levelled the tie in the 73rd minute with a low drive to beat Rangers keeper Ivor Pandur.There were no more goals which brought penalties, and although Pandur saved from Filip Zorvan, Curtis fired his spot-kick over the bar. James Penrice was then thwarted by Jablonec keeper Jan Hanus, leaving Jan Chramosta to fire in the decisive kick.The defeat is a huge blow to Rangers, who were knocked out of the Europa League qualifiers by Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok, losing 3-2 on aggregate. The club’s massive rebuild under McInnes is struggling to get off the ground, and now their European campaign is over in August.“I’m embarrassed with the performance,” McInnes admitted. “It wasn’t a good performance at any stretch of the imagination. I’m not going to sit here and make any excuses whatsoever. It wasn’t good enough.”“I thought the opposition were better than us in most aspects of the game so we got what we deserved,” he added. “If we’d won it on penalties, we’d have taken it … but we’d have covered over the cracks, to be honest. I’m mortified by the performance.”Brightonbooked their place in the Conference League’s league phase with a comfortable 4-0 play-off victory over Tromsø at the Amex Stadium. Albion had work to do in Thursday evening’s second leg after failing to capitalise on 25 attempts at goal during last week’s goalless first-leg draw in Norway.Fabian Hürzeler’s side were far more ruthless on home soil, with first-half finishes from Charalampos Kostoulas, Maxim De Cuyper and Mats Wieffer putting them firmly in control of the tie. Olivier Boscagli added a deflected fourth late on to seal a place in Friday’s draw.View image in fullscreenCharalambos Kostoulas beats Jakob Haugaard in the Tromsø goal to put Brighton ahead.Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/ReutersMotherwellwere left to rue another costly red card as their European adventure ended with a 4-1 defeat away to Freiburg in the Conference League playoffs.A week after Martin Moormann’s sending off paved the way for last season’s Europa League finalists to win 3-1 in the first leg, Well had Jake Girdwood-Reich dismissed just before the hour mark with the second leg in Germany still level at 1-1.Emmanuel Longelo’s equaliser, following a blunder from home goalkeeper Mio Backhaus, cancelled out an early opener from Derry Scherhant. The visitors’ hopes of emerging unscathed from a formidable away trip were dashed as goals from Igor Matanovic, Cyriaque Irie and Keisuke Goto secured a 7-2 aggregate win.Miguel Chaiwa scored a stoppage-time own goal asHiberniansuffered Conference League playoff despair for the second year running in a 3-2 home defeat by Gent.After a goalless first leg in Belgium last week, Hibs looked on course to make it to the league phase for the first time after second-half goals from Jason Kerr and Felix Passlack overturned a stunning first-half opener from Gent’s teenage forward Josue Vergara.But Christian Burgess equalised in the 84th minute for the visitors, before Hibs midfielder Chaiwa slid the ball into his own net in stoppage time. That confirmed another agonising European exit after a 4-3 aggregate defeat by Legia Warsaw at the same stage last season.View image in fullscreenManuel Toledano’s late extra-time penalty condemned Larne to playoff defeat against Gibraltar’s Lincoln Red Imps.Photograph: Liam McBurney/PAThere was also late agony for Northern Ireland’sLarne, who let a two-goal aggregate lead slip in the last 10 minutes at home to Gibraltar’s Lincoln Red Imps. Leading 2-0 from the first leg, Larne kept the visitors at bay until the 82nd minute, but Kike Gómez and Manu Toledano struck in quick succession to level the tie at 2-2 overall.Montel Gibson was sent off for the hosts in the 87th minute, and although Larne came close to taking the tie to a penalty shootout, Toledano scored a spot-kick in the 121st minute to seal their fate.Shamrock Roversalso missed out on the Conference League’s main phase as they lost 1-0 at Finnish side KuPS to seal a 2-1 aggregate loss.Explore more on these topicsConference LeagueRangersMotherwellnewsShareReuse this content

title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 7: Crystal Palace | Crystal Palace Women | The Guardian
description: Jo Potter’s side charged to promotion and have brought in striker Bethany England as they bid to stay up
Author: Sophie Downey
Headline: Jo Potter’s side charged to promotion and have brought in striker Bethany England as they bid to stay up
Content: Aimee Everett celebrates promotion to the Women's Super League after Crystal Palace’s victory over Portsmouth in May. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/WSL/Getty ImagesJo Potter’s side charged to promotion and have brought in striker Bethany England as they bid to stay upBySophie DowneyThu 27 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 19.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGuardian writers’ predicted position:13th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)Last season’s position:2nd (WSL2)ProspectsCrystal Palace have been on arollercoaster over the past few seasons. An inaugural Women’s Super League campaign in 2024-25 brought relegation and the club secured top-flight football again a year later. They will hope their WSL experience gives them an advantage with important lessons learned.The nature of their promotion push under Jo Potter was nothing short of remarkable. An indifferent start had them languishing near the bottom but 12 wins in their last 14 games enabled them to pip Charlton to the second automatic promotion spot on the final day.They have recruited intelligently over the summer. The arrival of the prolific Bethany England was a statement, as was the loan signing of the France goalkeeper Pauline Peyraud-Magnin, and Molly Bartrip brings considerable defensive acumen. In Shannon O’Brien and Lexi Lloyd-Smith, Potter has brought in two young attacking players who have caught the eye and Teyah Goldie and Fuka Tsunoda arrive on loan with the hope of kickstarting their careers.Faith has also been put in the core of the side that got them back to the WSL, many of whom have been through all the ups and downs. Abbie Larkin, Ashleigh Weerden, Shae Yanez and Molly-Mae Sharpe are a few of those who have stuck by the club and been rewarded. There was, however, a blow at the start pre-season when it was revealed My Cato had sustained an anterior cruciate ligament injury.Palace’s start is a tricky one. Everton, Arsenal and Tottenham make up their opening three games, a real chance to test themselves against seasoned WSL sides and see where they are at.How they finished in the past five seasonsOff-field pictureThe women’s team have been fully integrated into Crystal Palace FC since 2022, rather than being made into a separate entity like some of their WSL counterparts. Woody Johnson, David Blitzer, Josh Harris and Steve Parish continue to invest in and support the women’s side. There is a little uncertainty around the whole club after reports in June that Johnson, Blitzer and Harris are keen to sell their combined stake of 79% but nothing has come to fruition.The managerPotter is widely regarded as one of the brightest young managers. The 41-year-old arrived at Palace last summer, joining from Rangers, where she had hit the ground running in her managerial career, winning back-to-back cup doubles and narrowly missing out on the SWPL titles on two occasions. She was widely credited at Rangers for the integration and development of several academy players into the senior setup. Potter had a prolific playing career. She won the FA Cup with Birmingham in 2012 and was part of the England squad that secured bronze at the 2015 Women’s World Cup.View image in fullscreenJo Potter is seen as one of the brightest young managers in the game.Photograph: Nigel Roddis/WSL/Getty ImagesStar signingEngland’s arrival was a significant coup. The 32-year-old striker brings a wealth of experience, leadership, quality and goals that will surely be invaluable to the team’s chances of survival. England is an out-and-out goalscorer and her WSL tally sits at 87 after spells at Doncaster Belles, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham. She won nine major trophies during her seven-year stint at Chelsea and sparked life into Spurs, proving pivotal to their successful attempt at avoiding relegation from the WSL in 2023.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionStat attackPalace won one home match in 2024-25 when they finished bottom of the WSL. They maintained more of a fortress last season, topping the second tier for points won at home. Keeping something of that form going will be crucial if they are to stay up.Graphic showing Crystal Palace had the best home record in Women’s Super League 2Set for a breakthroughLloyd-Smith will be one to keep an eye on, the England youngster adding more firepower to the team. The 23-year-old gets her first shot at top-flight football, signing a three-year deal after a successful two years with Bristol City, where she finished last season as the WSL 2 top scorer and the club’s young player of the year. A versatile and speedy attacking player, she can thrive anywhere across the frontline.What they say“Palace are an ambitious club. They’ve been in the WSL before, they’ve had two amazing promotions now, and I think you can see their investment in thewomen’s game. They’re really pushing to want to be among the best, and they’ve got amazing facilities … It’s a place where I hope that I can make a lot of good memories, score a lot of goals, and make some good history for the football club” –England on signing for PalaceWhere are they playing their home games?The Eagles will continue at Sutton United’s VBS Community Stadium, where they have played since the 2023-24 campaign. The club continue to work hard to make it an entertaining and affordable matchday for supporters, with a fan zone before the game, affordable pricing and alcohol allowed in the stands, with a dedicated drink-free zone. Select games will be played at Selhurst Park, the first coming against Tottenham on 20 September.Explore more on these topicsWSL season previews 2026-27Crystal Palace WomenfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Wallabies rotate forwards for Argentina Test as Suaalii settles for place on bench | Australia rugby union team | The Guardian
description: Coach Les Kiss has left out captain Harry Wilson and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii from the Wallabies XV to play Argentina in Jujuy this weekend
Author: Jack Snape
Headline: Coach Les Kiss has left out captain Harry Wilson and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii from the Wallabies XV to play Argentina in Jujuy this weekend
Content: Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii will start from the bench in the Wallabies’ Test against Argentina this weekend.Photograph: Kenta Harada/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJoseph-Aukuso Suaalii will start from the bench in the Wallabies’ Test against Argentina this weekend.Photograph: Kenta Harada/Getty ImagesAustralia rugby union teamWallabies rotate forwards for Argentina Test as Suaalii settles for place on benchCaptain Harry Wilson left out of team entirely for clash in JujuyReshaped pack ‘worthwhile exploring’, says coach Les KissJack SnapeThu 27 Aug 2026 19.51 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 20.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCoach Les Kiss has left out captain Harry Wilson and high-profile recruit Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii from the Wallabies XV to play Argentina in Jujuy this weekend as he seeks to develop more depth in the squad ahead of next year’s World Cup.Tighthead prop Allan Alaalatoa will captain the side for the sixth time in the absence of Wilson who, having been rested entirely, will be replaced in the starting line-up at No 8 by Rob Valetini.Les Kiss reaps rewards of derring-do approach to Australia’s team selectionRead moreThe entire forward pack has been rotated followingthe 56-17 victory over Japanin Townsville two weeks ago, and prop Isaac Kailea comes in to play his first Test since 2024.Kiss said he and his staff have “tried to find out how deep we can go in each position” in the front row, while they have “reshaped” the pack this weekend because they think it’s “worthwhile exploring”.“It may not seem like order from you what you’re seeing, but it’s making sense internally with the players in particular why we’re doing those things,” he said.There is stability in the backline, however, with Ryan Lonergan again partnering Carter Gordon in the halves, and the back three of Max Jorgensen, Harry Potter and Tom Wright starting for a fourth straight match.The centre pairing of Hunter Paisami and Isaac Henry has also been retained, meaning Suaalii – who has recovered from a minor hamstring strain – will start from the bench.“We feel that there’s an opportunity to just maintain some continuity in that midfield that we did [have] with Carter [Gordon] and Lonners [Lonergan] there, and the back three, just to keep that in its right place and then utilise Joseph in any way that we wish from that position in terms of the positions he can cover,” Kiss said.“Likely 13 at this stage is the position he’ll cover, because we know Zac [Isaac Henry] can go to 12 if we need to as well, so that’s just trying to use our resources in different ways.”Wright said he did not have any preference about where he would like to see Suaalii come on and play. “I think you guys, the external guys [the media], all of you are entitled to your opinion, and well, I’ll leave you guys to have exactly that.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe fullback added, however, that he understood why there was such a focus on the rugby league import. “He’s obviously one of the bigger names in all of world rugby, arguably, he’s always going to be a talking point,” he said.“From my perspective, as one of his teammates in all five, six of the Tests that we’ve had this year, I think he’s been awesome for us. He works extremely hard during the week and he’s one of the most professional guys I’ve trained and played with.“So I probably see the other side of all the work that he puts into his game each week and the effect that he has on us as a team and all of his teammates.”Australia team: 15 Tom Wright, 14 Max Jorgensen, 13 Isaac Henry, 12 Hunter Paisami, 11 Harry Potter, 10 Carter Gordon, 9 Ryan Lonergan; 8 Rob Valetini, 7 Fraser McReight, 6 Tom Hooper, 5 Jeremy Williams, 4 Josh Canham, 3 Allan Alaalatoa (captain), 2 Brandon ​Paenga-Amosa, 1 Isaac Kailea.Replacements: 16 Billy Pollard, 17 Angus Bell, 18 Massimo de Lutiis, 19 Lachlan Shaw, ​20 Charlie Cale, 21Tate McDermott, ⁠22 Ben Donaldson, 23 Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii.Explore more on these topicsAustralia rugby union teamArgentina rugby union teamRugby unionAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Australia’s Nicola Olyslagers soars back to form on spectacular Diamond League night | Athletics | The Guardian
description: Australia’s world high jump champion Nicola Olyslagers has soared again on a sensational night of athletics in Zurich when two world records were broken
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Australia’s world high jump champion Nicola Olyslagers has soared again on a sensational night of athletics in Zurich when two world records were broken
Content: Nicola Olyslagers won the women's high jump final at the Weltklasse Zurich Diamond League meet at Stadion Letzigrund.Photograph: Sona Maleterova/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenNicola Olyslagers won the women's high jump final at the Weltklasse Zurich Diamond League meet at Stadion Letzigrund.Photograph: Sona Maleterova/Getty ImagesAthleticsAustralia’s Nicola Olyslagers soars back to form on spectacular Diamond League nightHigh jump world champion wins gold at prestigious meet in ZurichCam Myers impresses again in men’s 3000m with third placeAustralian Associated PressThu 27 Aug 2026 19.18 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNicola Olyslagers soared back to her world champion best at the Zurich Weltklasse meeting, but even the Australian high jump great was eclipsed on a spectacular night whentwo world records were smashed.Alison dos Santos shattered the world mark in the men’s ‌400m hurdles, breaking a five-year old mark of 45.94, while ‌Masai Russell blazed ‌to a ‌world record in the women’s 100m hurdles, clocking 12.09sec to eclipse the previous mark of 12.12.USA’s Russell and Brazil’s Dos Santos smash world records on ‘crazy’ night in ZurichRead moreThe most prestigious Diamond League meeting, which has long had the reputation of being the “two-hour Olympics” because of its quality, even looked as if it might deliver a third world record on the night as pole vault aces Armand Duplantis and Emmanouil Karalis both had a crack at 6.32 metres.Amid this landmark fare, Olyslagers may have been just a bit-part player but after a disappointing season in which she lost her Commonwealth title to teammate Eleanor Patterson, she roared back to her best form with a season’s best 2.02 metres to win by two centimetres from Ukrainian Iryna Gerashchenko.Patterson and Ukraine’s Olympic champion Yaroslava Mahuchikh both cleared 1.96m and had to settle for fourth and joint-sixth places respectively.Olyslagers revealed afterwards her victory had been down to ditching a new run-up which she finally decided at the weekend wasn’t working.“It took me some time to reflect,” she said after another disappointing outing in Poland at the weekend. “I decided it does not work, so within four days, I had to try to relearn in my head what I did last year to jump my lifetime best 2.04m here.“When I felt the track, I knew it was the same feeling as last year in the street meet. After I cleared two metres at the first attempt, I knew I was in shape. It was amazing.”View image in fullscreenOlyslagers clears the bar in Zurich.Photograph: Denis Balibouse/ReutersAmong other excellent Australian performances, Cam Myers got involved in the shake-up in the 3000m, clocking 7:27.97, but ending up pipped in the denouement by American duo Parker Wolfe (meeting record 7:27.43) and Graham Blanks (7:27.92).“It was a tough race, the people out there are strong competitors,” Myers said. “I knew it was going to be a good test, but in the end Parker was just better than me, that’s how it goes.”Jess Hull, fifth in 1:58.24, tested her speed out in a lightning 800m won in dazzling fashion by Swiss heroine Audrey Werro, who clocked a world-leading 1:53.70.Torrie Lewis was second in a non-Diamond League 200 metres, clocking just outside her season’s best in 22.66sec behind Swiss winner Fabienne Hoenke (22.53).Explore more on these topicsAthleticsAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester City target Iliman Ndiaye but Everton value forward at £80m | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Manchester City have identified Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye as a potential target following the £75m departure of Sávio to Tottenham
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Manchester City have identified Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye as a potential target following the £75m departure of Sávio to Tottenham
Content: Iliman Ndiaye has 44 caps for Senegal and has impressed for Everton since joining the club from Marseille in July 2024.Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenIliman Ndiaye has 44 caps for Senegal and has impressed for Everton since joining the club from Marseille in July 2024.Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesManchester CityManchester City target Iliman Ndiaye but Everton value forward at £80mEverton interested in taking Grealish back from CityOmar Marmoush joins Spurs in season-long loanJamie JacksonandAndy HunterThu 27 Aug 2026 18.17 EDTFirst published on Thu 27 Aug 2026 07.22 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleManchester City have identified Iliman Ndiaye as a potential target after the£75m departure of Sávio to TottenhamEverton value the wide forward in the region of £80m.With Omar Marmoush also joining Spurs, on an initial season-long loan,Enzo Marescawants to strengthen his attacking options. He is an admirer of Ndiaye, who has played 44 times for Senegal and is contracted to Everton until 2029.‘I can’t wait’: Liam Delap seals £45m Nottingham Forest move from ChelseaRead moreEverton are interested in bringing Jack Grealish back from City after having him on loan last season. Grealish, alsoon Sunderland’s list of targets, is in the final year of his deal and Maresca suggested on Thursday the 30-year-old would leave.“Jack is here until the day that he’s not here,” he said. “It’s my duty to try to help him to give us the best and then we’ll see in the next four-five days what happens.”City agreed a €37.5m (£34m) deal for the Palmeiras winger Allan Elias on Monday, and are monitoring Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo.Maresca said City were also aiming to add “one or two captains” before the transfer window closes on Tuesday night. This summer, City’s squad has lost the leadership and experience of Bernardo Silva,Rodri,John Stonesand Nathan Aké.Maresca has nominated Rúben Dias and Erling Haaland as captains, but wants to add more players who can fill the role. One the Italian has identified is Enzo Fernández, who has captained Chelsea.Although Chelsea’sdeadline of 14 Augustfor a bid to be lodged passed without one, City are expected to move for the 25-year-old midfielder. The targeting of Fernández follows the departures of Rodri and Nico González.Maresca spoke generally about leadership. “We have experienced players,” he said. “For sure, we have leaders. Now we need to wait four-five more days when the transfer window closes if we can add one or two more captains to Rúben and Erling.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMaresca started Phil Foden inSunday’s 2-1 win over Bournemouth, fielding him on the wing rather than his more familiar No 10 position, because Jérémy Doku is injured. Foden has been inconsistent in the past two seasons. “For sure he can give much more,” Maresca said. “No doubt that he is going to be, again, the Phil we all know and we all want.”Maresca downplayed Foden’s ability to be a captain, but said: “Because many players left, he has to take one step forward in terms of personality, leadership. But since day one I’ve been very happy with the way he’s working, and also his mood – he’s happy.”Matheus Nunes is a doubt for City’s trip to Crystal Palace on Friday.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityEnzo MarescaEvertonTransfer windownewsShareReuse this content

title: Broad and Anderson lament ‘extreme and tiresome’ off-field incidents involving England players | Stuart Broad | The Guardian
description: Stuart Broad and Jimmy ­Anderson have criticised the ‘extreme and tiresome’ flood of negative ­stories around the England cricket team’s drinking and socialising habits
Author: Simon Burnton
Headline: Stuart Broad and Jimmy ­Anderson have criticised the ‘extreme and tiresome’ flood of negative ­stories around the England cricket team’s drinking and socialising habits
Content: A portrait of England bowlers James Anderson and Stuart Broad in the Long Room at Lord’s.Photograph: Gareth Copley/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenA portrait of England bowlers James Anderson and Stuart Broad in the Long Room at Lord’s.Photograph: Gareth Copley/Getty ImagesStuart BroadBroad and Anderson lament ‘extreme and tiresome’ off-field incidents involving England players‘Mind-numbing that people end up in these positions’Brydon Carse incident is the latest in a long lineSimon Burntonat Lord'sThu 27 Aug 2026 16.46 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 19.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleStuart Broad and Jimmy Anderson have criticised the “extreme and tiresome” flood of negative stories around the England cricket team’s drinking and socialising habits, with Anderson – England’s all-time leading wicket-taker – saying it is “just mind-numbing that people can still be putting themselves in these positions”.The latest scandal involving members of the Test squad involved the bowler Brydon Carse, who was pictured being led away from a Derby bar in handcuffs in the early hours of Sunday morning. The 31-year-old was briefly arrested by police on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly before being “de-arrested”, though they continue to investigate an allegation of assault in connection with the incident. Carse was dropped from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan that started at Lord’s on Thursday, buttook two wickets for Durhamon the first day of their County Championship game against Gloucestershire.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAbbas dusts himself down to dominate England – and close in on the honours board | Simon BurntonRead more“Eight of the 30 centrally contracted players have now been reprimanded or involved and that is quite extreme and actually quite tiresome,” Broad said, at the unveiling of a joint portrait of himself and Anderson at Lord’s on Wednesday night. “Joe Root spoke beautifully on this and is a brilliant example of how to do it. If you won’t listen to him and follow him, then this is not for you. South Africa away [this winter] and Australia at home [next summer] – if you can’t commit every bit of your mind and body to wanting to perform on this field, then I don’t understand.”Anderson was one of several players fined for a breach of discipline at a nightclub in St Lucia during the 2007 World Cup, when he was 24. “I learned my lesson the hard way early on,” he said. “You learn from it and I said to myself: ‘Right, I’m not going out for the next two years.’ It was a massive wake-up call. You can make a mistake when you’re young, but you have to learn from it and grow up fast. So it’s just mind-numbing that people can still be putting themselves in these positions when there is so much attention around it.”Anderson went on to play 401 games for England across all formats, before retiring from international cricket in 2024 aged 41. He continues to play for Lancashire. “We went through our careers. People messed up and we were no angels – we enjoyed a beer and celebrated victory as hard as anyone,” he said. “But when we were successful, we had players who did that sort of policing. Someone would say: ‘Just come away, you don’t need another drink, you don’t need to go to a nightclub,’ and if someone wasn’t training properly someone would say to them: ‘You tossed off that net session, you didn’t practise properly.’ This is a young team and they’ll get there.”Explore more on these topicsStuart BroadJimmy AndersonEngland cricket teamEngland v Pakistan 2026CricketnewsShareReuse this content

title: Pakistan complain to Sky after interview with Imran Khan’s sons over father’s treatment | England v Pakistan 2026 | The Guardian
description: The Pakistan Cricket Board has made a formal complaint to Sky Sports after it broadcast an interview with Imran Khan’s sons, Kasim and Sulaiman, during its coverage of the first day’s play at Lord’s
Author: Ali Martin
Headline: The Pakistan Cricket Board has made a formal complaint to Sky Sports after it broadcast an interview with Imran Khan’s sons, Kasim and Sulaiman, during its coverage of the first day’s play at Lord’s
Content: Imran Khan in 2023. His family have expressed concerns about his health.Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/ReutersView image in fullscreenImran Khan in 2023. His family have expressed concerns about his health.Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/ReutersEngland v Pakistan 2026Pakistan complain to Sky after interview with Imran Khan’s sons over father’s treatmentFormer captain in solitary confinement since 2023Tourists threatened to refuse to return to field after lunchMatt HughesandAli MartinThu 27 Aug 2026 16.21 EDTFirst published on Thu 27 Aug 2026 13.18 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Pakistan Cricket Board made a formal complaint to Sky Sports after it broadcast an interview with Imran Khan’s sons, Kasim and Sulaiman, during its coverage of the first day’s play at Lord’s. The tourists were so incensed that Babar Azam’s side threatened to refuse to return to the field after lunch.During the interview with Sky’s Michael Atherton, Khan’s children raised concerns about the Pakistan government’s treatment of the country’s former prime minister, including the claim that they are “trying to kill him”.Jailed ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan allowed brief hospital visit after uproar over healthRead moreKhan has been in solitary confinement for three years. Lawyers have described his living conditions as slow-motion murder, his sister claimed he has been tortured and 21 former cricketers including Atherton have campaigned for him to be treated humanely.The PCB was unhappy with Sky, which is a long-term rights partner of the England and WalesCricketBoard, giving the Khans airtime and is understood to have lobbied for the interview not to be broadcast. The chair of the PCB, Mohsin Naqvi, is also Pakistan’s minister of the interior and is extremely close to the government.Sky refused to back down, however, and after the interview was broadcast during the rain-delayed lunch break PCB officials briefly threatened to stop their players from returning. The ECB succeeded in talking them round during tense discussions and the afternoon and evening sessions took place as planned before bad light stopped play just before 6pm.Pakistan remain aggrieved, though, and are understood to have also raised the issue with the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. Discussions with the touring party were continuing on Thursday night, with the ECB having received assurances that Pakistan will take the field on day two.During the interview Kasim Khan said: “It is not very clear what they are doing, just blatantly trying to kill him in there. Keep him in as long as possible and silence him.”The 73-year-old was moved to a hospital last week for treatment after a supreme court ruling permitted his temporary release, but has since been returned to prison.In addition to his family, Khan’s plight has also been highlighted by many of the world’s great former cricketers, who have written two joint letters calling “for humane treatment and proper medical care”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAfter publishing their first letter in February the group, which includes six former England captains, former India captain Kapil Dev and Australian players Adam Gilchrist and Greg Chappell, issued another this week calling for “a full and independent assessment of his health”, particularly on his right eye.Khan’s lawyers have said he has lost 85% of vision in his right eye as a result of his living conditions.Sky, the ECB and the PCB declined to comment.Explore more on these topicsEngland v Pakistan 2026Imran KhanEngland cricket teamPakistan cricket teamCricketnewsShareReuse this content

title: Carse in the wickets for Durham, Surrey struggle again – as it happened | County Championship | The Guardian
description: County Championship day one: Brydon Carse took two early wickets as Durham took the upper hand against Gloucestershire while Sam Cook led the way for Essex against Surrey
Author: Tanya Aldred
Headline: County Championship day one: Brydon Carse took two early wickets as Durham took the upper hand against Gloucestershire while Sam Cook led the way for Essex against Surrey
Content: 10h ago14.40 EDTRoundup: Carse gets back down to business, Surrey toil againDurham’s Brydon Carse, last pictured in handcuffs outside a Derby nightclub and subsequently dropped from England’s Test squad, took his emotions out onGloucestershireearly. He truncheoned Joe Phillips’s middle stump with his sixth ball and induced Miles Hammond into a flamboyant drive by a couple of overs later. With Matthew Potts snaffling Cameron Bancroft, Gloucestershire were on the precipice at 13 for three. A classy 60 from James Bracey enabled them to limp to 137, but Kasey Aldridge mopped up most of the rest with five for 16. Durham then lost two quick wickets, until an unbeaten half-century from David Bedingham sailed them to calmer waters.It was another dud day forSurreyon what is turning into a miserable Championship summer. After losing the toss and being asked to bat, they were soon in trouble on a verdant Chelmsford wicket. Sam Cook, who swapped into theEssexside after being released by England, picked up three wickets alongside Zaman Akhter, as Surrey were dismissed for 183. Adam Thomas top scored with 43, but there were few consolation runs for Ollie Pope, also surplus to requirements at Lord’s. There was just time for Essex’s Paul Walter to be caught behind before bad light stopped play.Honours were fairly even at North Marine Road where the rain blew in mid-afternoon.Leicestershire’s Josh Davey plucked out bothYorkshireopeners cheaply, but Sam Whiteman and James Wharton, unbeaten on 70, restocked the shelves. Jonny Bairstow flashed hazardly and was caught behind for one, to Scarborough sighs.Zak Crawley’s highest score of the season gaveKenta boost on a long day waiting for the rain to stop at Wantage Road. His unbeaten 82 dominated an unbroken opening stand of 154 with Ben Compton in the promotion nose to nose againstNorthamptonshire.Sonny Baker ripped upGlamorgan’s rebuilding plans, with two wickets in his first over after being subbed into theHampshireside. It was a typically Tiggerish entrance on a damp day designed for bowlers – 17 wickets fell, including Glamorgan’s top three all for ducks.Sussex’s Henry Crocombe grabbed a hat-trick at Hove asSomersetlost their last five wickets for 11 runs.Share

title: ‘Grand slams are the engine to make a living’: Mackenzie McDonald on why players still compete when injured | Tennis | The Guardian
description: Mackenzie McDonald tells Matt Hughes about life on the professional circuit and those making sacrifices for a pay cheque
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Mackenzie McDonald tells Matt Hughes about life on the professional circuit and those making sacrifices for a pay cheque
Content: Mackenzie McDonald has played on the ATP Tour for 10 years and reached the world’s top 60 in 2019.Photograph: Aaron Favila/APView image in fullscreenMackenzie McDonald has played on the ATP Tour for 10 years and reached the world’s top 60 in 2019.Photograph: Aaron Favila/APTennisInterview‘Grand slams are the engine to make a living’: Mackenzie McDonald on why players still compete when injuredMatt HughesAmerican talks life on the professional circuit and those making sacrifices for a pay cheque, often compromising physical and mental welfareThu 27 Aug 2026 10.27 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 16.17 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFor Mackenzie McDonald the players’ push for greater prize money and welfare contributions from the grand slam tournaments could result in the difference between putting food on the table and making a decent living.After 10 years on the ATP Tour the 31-year-old American is not pleading poverty, but knows that life on the professional circuit can be a hand-to-mouth existence, with players’ physical and mental welfare often compromised due to their desperation to get back on court.Players welcome record $108m US Open prize fund and will not stage protestsRead moreMcDonald keeps returning to the point that many of his peers at the US Open will be playing despite carrying serious injuries because of their need for a pay cheque.With first-round losers in the men’s and women’s singles receiving a record $140,000 (£103,000) many will not blame them, although in a sport with a more coherent financial structure and generous welfare provision such sacrifices might not be necessary.Despite combined annual revenues of more than $2bn the four grand slams do not provide a formal contribution to player welfare or pensions, although the US Tennis Association (USTA) made a significant step last week bycommitting $2m to a new player support programme.“I know a good handful of players right now that are seriously hurt,” McDonald says. “But I know they’re going to show up to the US Open and get on court to make sure they can make some money because they’ve got bills to pay. They want to get an apartment and they want to pay their team – a coach, physio, trainer.“The grand slams are the engine that enables them to make a living and they have to capitalise on that. It’s the difference between putting food on the table and making a living. That’s what’s at stake for some people.”Much of the lobbying for the slams to increase their prize pots to 22% of revenues, from the current position of about 15%, has come fromglobal stars such as Jannik Sinner and Aryna Sabalenkadue to their public profile, but McDonald provides a more compelling case than the gripes of multimillionaires.With total earnings of more than $7m he is unlikely to be on the bread line at present, but has been at various points in his career. Seemingly high income levels ignore the fact that players are responsible for their travel and coaching costs, plus those of their often large entourages.“Things have shifted, but at the lower level the money has always been pretty insignificant,” McDonald says. “I’d say if you’re ranked 250 in the world right now you’re making about $200,000. I know for a fact that only 88 players last year made a million dollars. But that’s before taxes and all your costs, which are very significant.“Many players go straight from college, where everything is paid for, into professional tennis where you’re booking your own flights and often paying for premium flights at the end of the week.“I became a master of travel cheat codes, but you also have to pay for your performance team, whether that’s a strength and conditioning coach, a physio, psychologist or your main coach. Plus their travel.View image in fullscreenMackenzie McDonald is fit to play at the US Open if he comes through qualifying, but has also experienced the darker side of tennis.Photograph: Sipa US/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.“As players, we’re an undervalued asset for how much screen time we provide for broadcasters and how much betting income we generate for gambling operators.”McDonald is fit to play at Flushing Meadows if he comes through qualifying, but has also experienced the darker side of a sport with comprehensive medical insurance limited to the world’s top 150 players, although the next 100 are given a more basic package by the ATP.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAfter breaking into the world’s top 60 for the first time in 2019 he missed most of the season after sustaining a serious hamstring injury at the French Open. His comeback was derailed by the Covid-19 pandemic the following year.“The tough part about tennis is that when you get hurt you’re not making any money and your world ranking also goes down, which limits your ability to compete in the future,” McDonald says. “You can’t just get back on the wheel.“I went from being young and hungry to sitting in my apartment not being able to walk and trying to pick up the pieces to get a pay cheque again. I was lucky that it was 2019 and the medics had the knowledge of how to fix the injury.“Being able to adapt to how you’re doing is a skill in itself. You could have a really good year and make say seven figures, but then you get injured and you’re not earning anything.‘You start all over’: Linda Noskova battles fame and desire after Wimbledon gloryRead more“If you saw the shit we deal with on a daily basis it’s pretty comical. This year I’ve lost my bag multiple times and had to fly around the world with no possessions. If you get off the hamster wheel you’re not making money. When you’re on the hamster wheel you’ve got to keep going. It’s pretty brutal.”The USTA’s commitment to creating a player support programme as part of this year’s $108m prize fund is a significant development, which has led the players to cancel plans to repeat themedia boycottthat overshadowed the start of the French Open, but the long-running dispute has not been resolved.In addition to wanting a similar undertaking from the other slams, the players’ representatives are demanding a fixed revenue-share scheme be implemented.“I hope in the future that the money-making engines of tennis would help to contribute to player welfare,” McDonald says. “It’s going in that direction, but how fast it happens is a different question.”Explore more on these topicsTennisUS Open Tennis 2026US Open tennisUS sportsinterviewsShareReuse this content

title: Can the Philly Classic ignite another golden age of US road cycling? | Cycling | The Guardian
description: The race was at its peak when American riders were regularly challenging for titles. Its return could help prompt a revival
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The race was at its peak when American riders were regularly challenging for titles. Its return could help prompt a revival
Content: The Philly Classic takes in notable locations such as the city’s art museum.Photograph: Chris Boswell/AlamyView image in fullscreenThe Philly Classic takes in notable locations such as the city’s art museum.Photograph: Chris Boswell/AlamyCyclingCan the Philly Classic ignite another golden age of US road cycling?The race was at its peak when American riders were regularly challenging for titles. Its return could help prompt a revivalMichael Venutolo-MantovaniThu 27 Aug 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 11.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAfter a decade-long absence, the belovedPhiladelphiaInternational Cycling Classic is set to return this weekend, with some of the world’s best bike-racing teams taking to the famous circuit around the city’s leafy Art Museum, Manayunk, and Roxborough areas on Sunday.The race is one of just a handful of events on American soil sanctioned by UCI, cycling’s international governing body, and will feature squads such as EF Education EasyPost, Lidl-Trek, Lotto-Intermarché, and Jayco AlUla in the men’s race, and powerhouses CANYON//SRAM zondacrypto and Human Powered Health in the women’s event. It is classified as a 1.1 race, meaning it’s two levels below the top-flight WorldTour, whose races include the Tour de France, Paris-Roubaix, and Liège-Bastogne-Liège.The race will retrace its celebrated 14.4-mile loop, starting on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway, roaring past the city’s famous art museum, snaking along the Schuykill River, through Fairmount Park, and into the Manayunk neighborhood, where the race’s most famous segment awaits. It’s a short but brutal climb, known as “The Wall,” that averages a leg-crushing 17% of incline and has become synonymous with the Philly Classic. So synonymous in fact, that Manayunk officially designated the stretch of road as the “Manayunk Wall” in 2002.After tackling The Wall, the racers will head back toward the Ben Franklin Parkway only to do it all over again. The men’s peloton will complete eight laps of the circuit, totaling 124 miles. The women will complete 62 miles. Those distance totals make a bit more sense on the metric scale, as they equal 200km and 100km, respectively.Beyond the headline-grabbing rebirth of this famous American race,the new iteration of the Philly Classic is being lauded for offering equal prize money for both the men’s and women’s races. At $75,000 each for both the men’s and women’s races, the total prize money is double the minimum for a UCI race at this level. However, parity is nothing new for this race, which offered equal prizes as far back as 2013.Lisa Nutter, a world champion track cyclist and the wife of Philadelphia’s mayor, originally pushed for equal pay between the genders.“Mayor [Michael] and Lisa Nutter were very adamant that we should have prize parity back then,” the race’s director, Robin Morton, said. “And so, we felt that we needed to continue that tradition and make sure the men and the women got paid the same.”The race, which originally ran from 1985 to 2016 (with a women’s race being added in 1994, known as the “Liberty Classic” through 2012),hit its zenith in stride with the rest of American cycling. That is to say, around the time Lance Armstrong was winning seven Tours de France, all of which were vacated after Armstrong admitted to doping. That era was not only the result of Armstrong’s dominance and subsequent fame but also of the seeds that were planted in American cycling in the 1980s, thanks to the success of racers such as Greg LeMond, a three-time winner of the Tour de France, and Ohio native Andy Hampsten, who won the 1988 Giro d’Italia.It was in the early 1980s that the United States began to foster a domestic racing scene, eventually hosting marquee races such as the Coors Classic, the Ore-Ida Women’s Challenge, the Tour de Georgia, the San Francisco Grand Prix, the Tour of California and of course, the Philly Classic.Past winners of the men’s race include 11-time-Tour de France stage winner André Greipel, Armstrong, American cycling legend George Hincapie, and 1995 American national champion Norm Alvis. The women’s race was dominated in the late 1990s and early 2000s by five-time winner and Olympic gold medalist Petra Rossner, and counts two-time world champion Giorgia Bronzini and American standout Evelyn Stevens as past winners.Today, the United States hosts just a few UCI-sanctioned road races: the Redlands Bicycle Classic, the Tour of the Gila, the MarylandCyclingClassic, and the Tour of Arkansas, formerly known as the Joe Martin Stage Race.Adding the Philadelphia International Cycling Classic to that list is a huge step forward for American cycling, which has shifted its focus from road racing toward criterium racing and gravel racing over the last two decades. Or maybe it’s more accurate to say it’s a huge step backwards, to that brief stretch in American sports history when cycling was at its peak and the US was a major player on the world scene.The Philadelphia Cycling Classic will be livestreamed on Channel 6 ABC, with the women’s race kicking off at 8.30am Eastern. The men will follow at 12.30pm. Of course, you could always trek to Philly and become part of the party yourself. I highly recommend snagging a spot somewhere along The Wall.Explore more on these topicsCyclingPhiladelphiaUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Muchová and Menšík win $1m US Open mixed doubles title in late-night thriller | US Open Tennis 2026 | The Guardian
description: Czech pair cap two-day mixed doubles spectacle with $1m title as revamped event strengthens the US Open’s three-week ambitions
Author: Ella Brockway
Headline: Czech pair cap two-day mixed doubles spectacle with $1m title as revamped event strengthens the US Open’s three-week ambitions
Content: The Czech duo of Karolína Muchová and Jakub Menšík lift the trophy after defeating Belinda Bencic of Switzerland and Flavio Cobolli of Italy in the US Open mixed doubles final.Photograph: Timothy A Clary/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe Czech duo of Karolína Muchová and Jakub Menšík lift the trophy after defeating Belinda Bencic of Switzerland and Flavio Cobolli of Italy in the US Open mixed doubles final.Photograph: Timothy A Clary/AFP/Getty ImagesUS Open Tennis 2026Muchová and Menšík win $1m US Open mixed doubles title in late-night thrillerCzech pair beat Bencic and Cobolli in deciding tiebreakRevamped event draws strong crowds at Arthur AsheSingles stars dominate after doubles specialists exitElla Brockwayat Flushing MeadowsThu 27 Aug 2026 00.15 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 08.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTo many who came to the US Open grounds this week, the showpiece of the mixed doubles championshipcameTuesday afternoon, with the returns of Serena Williams (after four years away from tennis) and Carlos Alcaraz (after four months out with a wrist injury).To the players who remained in the field after Williams and Alcaraz exited in the quarter-finals, the real highlight was Wednesday night’s final at Arthur Ashe Stadium, with its $1m in prize money on the line. Karolína Muchová and Jakub Menšík made the most of the spotlight, beating Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli 6-3, 1-6 (10-6) for the title.Serena and Venus Williams will play doubles together at the US OpenRead moreTheir win capped an event that, in a reversal of recent years, was dominated by singles players instead of doubles specialists. The Czech duo beat Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev 5-4 (8-6) 3-5 (11-9) and the runners-up bested Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils 4-5 (7-9) 4-1 (10-5) in a pair of competitive semi-finals that each lasted over an hour, making for a final that finished just before midnight.“This format of a tournament, it went really quickly,” said Muchová, who was playing her first matches sincelosing the Wimbledon finalin July. “I’m obviously super happy that we managed to win. It was not my expectation.”Since its format was reimagined last year in an effort to entice the top singles players to participate, the mixed doubles competition has drawn criticism. Therevampmoved the tournament a week before the start of singles play and raised the winners’ prize from$200,000to $1m, but cut the field to 16 and drew outcry from doubles specialists kept out of the draw. The 2025 champions, Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori, were specialists, but some questioned whether the new event - with its four-game sets until the final, no ad-scoring and a 10-point tiebreak - should even be categorized as a grand slam title.Tournament organizers responded this year, adjusting the format to include an eight-team qualifying draw that allowed more specialists to enter. They gathered a captivating field, headlined by Williams playing in New York for the first time since the 2022 match that washer presumptive farewell. Even so, by Tuesday’s end, the tournament had lost not just its highest-profile names - Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka and Felix Auger-Aliassime andAlex Ealamade quick first-round exits - but also its doubles specialist teams, all four of whom were out by the quarter-finals.View image in fullscreenKarolína Muchová and Jakub Menšík celebrate a point during Wednesday’s match.Photograph: Caleb Bowlin/Getty ImagesWhat the semi-finalist pairs lacked in spectacle or doubles pedigree, they made up for in another category: bringing the fun that this format encouraged. Asked how they’d spend the time before the final, Bencic answered “beer”, earning a laugh and slight panic from Cobolli. Muchová and Menšík played their matches in color-coordinated pink-and-maroon looks; when Muchová first floated the idea for their outfits, Menšík had to ask what maroon was. Andreeva joked she used to have a crush on the nine-years-older Rublev.As for Monfils and Svitolina, few pairs in the sport know each other better: they married in 2021 and have a three-year-old daughter, but had never played doubles together before this week. While Svitolina is the world No 9, the 307th-ranked Monfils is set to retire after this season and received a singles wild card. Neither has ever advanced past a semi-final at a grand slam.They carried the momentum of their first two wins into Wednesday’s semi-final, winning an even first set in a tiebreak by holding serve and forcing long rallies. At 7-7 in the tiebreak, Bencic’s backhand hit her out-of-position partner, and Cobolli then double-faulted to end the set.The Italian wore his frustration as Monfils and Svitolina held for the first game of the second set. He double-faulted his opening serve, but he recovered to save triple break point in a moment that became a turning point for their championship hopes. He and Bencic had the night’s first break in the third game, again from three points down, and two games later broke Monfils without resistance to take the set. As the match pushed past an hour, Monfils and Svitolina ran out of steam – even as the Ashe crowd urged them on with its loudest cheers of the night – and Bencic and Cobolli won 21 of the final 26 points.The second semi-final was even more evenly matched. Behind the 6ft 5in Menšík’s aggressive net play and Muchová’s strong returns, the Czech duo won the first set in an 8-6 tiebreak, a graceful backhanded volley by Muchova securing it. Andreeva and Rublev took their turn in the second, sending winners down the alleys and forcing the Czechs to work for points.View image in fullscreenKarolína Muchová and Jakub Menšík speak after winning the US Open mixed doubles final over Switzerland’s Belinda Bencic and Italy’s Flavio Cobolli.Photograph: Brendan McDermid/ReutersThe back-and-forth continued in the tiebreak before Muchová and Menšík – with the help of Menšík’s big serve – erased two match points and ran off the final four points.The Czechs had just 17 minutes to recover before their late-night final. At first, the lack of a break didn’t seem to much affect them – they took the first set behind eight winners and Menšík’s four aces. But Bencic and Cobolli, as they had earlier, grabbed a wave of momentum in the second set, breaking a wobbly Muchová to go up 4-1 before Bencic’s cross-court forehand in the seventh game sent the match to a tiebreak.Muchová and Menšík delivered clutch points on their final serves late in the tiebreak; Bencic and Cobolli netted three of four, and Menšík’s seventh ace of the night on triple championship point won it.The crowd had significantly thinned by the time the duo lifted their trophy, but the earlier turnout seemed proof the US Open has made itself a three-week event. Ashe was mostly full for Wednesday’s semi-finals. The stadium was packed a night earlier for a pair of exhibition matches honoring Roger Federer, featuring the likes of Andy Roddick, John McEnroe, Andre Agassi and the 20-time major winner himself.Throughout their mixed doubles run, the Czechs said their focus remained on the singles draw. Muchová, the world No 6, has reached two major finals and the semi-finals in New York; Menšík, enjoying a career-best season, will seek to advance past the third round here for the first time. Singles play begins Sunday. The road to another title on Ashe will be more difficult, but the pair – and the tournament’s organizers – will surely see this week as a welcome prelude.“We had really great matches to play,” said Menšík, who had never played mixed doubles before this week. “It’s a pretty different discipline [from singles, but] at the same time it’s good that we tried a lot of things on the court. So, of course, it gives you a little bit of boost of confidence.”Explore more on these topicsUS Open Tennis 2026TennisUS Open tennisUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Roger Goodell says NFL is reviewing Jed York’s arrest under personal conduct policy | San Francisco 49ers | The Guardian
description: Roger Goodell says the NFL is reviewing whether the 49ers owner should face discipline after his arrest in an Ohio prostitution sting
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Roger Goodell says the NFL is reviewing whether the 49ers owner should face discipline after his arrest in an Ohio prostitution sting
Content: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested on Sunday in East Palestine, Ohio, and pleaded guilty on Monday to two misdemeanors.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PAView image in fullscreenSan Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested on Sunday in East Palestine, Ohio, and pleaded guilty on Monday to two misdemeanors.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PASan Francisco 49ersRoger Goodell says NFL is reviewing Jed York’s arrest under personal conduct policyGoodell confirms review after Ohio prostitution stingYork pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor chargesNFL has previously disciplined owners for misconductAgenciesWed 26 Aug 2026 22.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCommissioner Roger Goodell said the NFL is looking into whetherSan Francisco 49ersowner Jed York will be punished for violating the league’s personal conduct policy after he was caught in a prostitution sting in Ohio.“It’s being reviewed under the personal conduct policy,” Goodell said Wednesday at the owners’ meetings in Atlanta. “We’ll do that and when there’s something to be reported we’ll talk.”Jed York’s trailer park arrest exposed inequality in America | Lee EscobedoRead moreYorkwas arrested in a mobile home parkby the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force after police said he was attempting to pay $160 for sex with a woman he believed to be a prostitute.York was booked into jail and was released after posting a $5,000 bond. York was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. He pleaded no contest to that charge and to possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to the an undercover online prostitution advertisement.He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest. He also was fined $1,150. Police seized the $160 from York and that was later given to the human trafficking task force as part of the plea. York also completed an online course.York has spent most of the summer in Ohio, where he grew up near Youngstown. He had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May, according to court records.Owners have been previously punished for violating the personal conduct policy. The late Indianapolis Colts owner Jim Irsay was suspended for six games and fined $500,000 following a guilty plea to driving while impaired in 2014.New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft was investigated but not punished by the league after he was arrested in Florida in 2019 for allegedly paying for sex with a woman at a massage parlor. The chargewas later droppedafter a court ruled that police violated the rights of Kraft and the other customers when they secretly installed video cameras inside massage rooms at the spa.York was arrested on Sunday in East Palestine, Ohio, and pleaded guilty on Monday to two misdemeanors.Explore more on these topicsSan Francisco 49ersRoger GoodellNFLUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: UK expects Meta to match US child safety measures after $18bn settlement | Social media ban | The Guardian
description: Minister calls for Instagram owner to extend sweeping new safeguards for young users to Britain
Author: Robert Booth
Headline: Minister calls for Instagram owner to extend sweeping new safeguards for young users to Britain
Content: The UK government expects the Instagram owner, Meta, to roll out the same protections for children in Britain.Photograph: Ekaterina Goncharova; posed by model/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe UK government expects the Instagram owner, Meta, to roll out the same protections for children in Britain.Photograph: Ekaterina Goncharova; posed by model/Getty ImagesSocial media banUK expects Meta to match US child safety measures after $18bn settlementMinister calls for Instagram owner to extend sweeping new safeguards for young users to BritainUK politics live – latest updatesBusiness live – latest updatesRobert BoothUK technology editorThu 27 Aug 2026 06.30 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 15.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe UK government expects the Instagram owner Meta to roll out the same protections for children in Britain asthose it agreed in the US on Wednesday, as part of a court settlement that could cost the company up to $18bn (£13bn).Pat McFadden, the work and pensions secretary, said on Thursday he did not want young people in the US to have “a higher rate of protection” than those in Britain, after Meta settled a lawsuit brought by dozens of US states accusing the company ofharming children with dangerous products.As well as the payouts, Meta agreed to a default daily time limit of two hours for users under 18 that can be lifted only by a parent – a measure not currently proposed underplans to ban social media for under-16sin the UK – and a default block between midnight and 6am for under-18s, as well as default blocks on user notifications at night and during the school day.Analysts have pointed out the measures largely fall within the bounds of changesMetahas already been required to make elsewhere. But restrictions agreed by Meta in the US that have not been proposed in the UK include bans on under-18s displaying numbers of likes or reactions and on cosmetic procedure image filters.Meta has urged TikTok and YouTube to adopt the same standards “to ensure teens use social media in a healthy and responsible way”.View image in fullscreenCountries around the world are beginning to restrict social media for children children’s access to social media amid rising concern about harms,Photograph: Yui Mok/PAAsked on Sky News whether he expected Meta to roll out the new safety features in the UK, McFadden said: “Yes, we would. We don’t want a situation where young people in America have got a higher rate of protection than young people in the UK.”In June, Keir Starmer’s government announced an Australia-styleban on social media for children under 16would come into force by early 2027. It also said in July thatdefault overnight curfews from midnight to 6am would be switched onfor 16- and 17-year-olds using social media apps, while features designed to keep users scrolling for longer would be switched off by default.McFadden said the social media ban for young people would come into force next year, confirmed the overnight curfews and added: “We’ve got to do something about this endless scrolling, which is so addictive for young people.”Countries around the world are beginning to restrict children’s access to social media amid rising concern about harms. In March, Indonesia began blocking children under 16 from accessing most social media. Malaysia followed suit in June. France passed a law banning social media access for under-15s in July, while Turkey passed a bill with similar restrictions. Bans or limits are beingconsidered by 19 other countries, according to the Tech Policy Press non-profit organisation.The Meta settlement announced on Wednesday cut short a trial in Oakland, California, in which lawyers for 29 US statesaccusedMetaof covering up internal research showing thatInstagramwas addictive for teenagers. Legal experts, including James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell University, described the settlement as “a sign of vulnerability on Meta’s part”. It also prompted calls for the UK government to tighten its grip on social media companies after critics said the2023 Online Safety Act, enforced by Ofcom, had had limited effect.The Molly Rose Foundation, set up by the father of Molly Russell, who took her own life in 2017 after falling into avortex of despair on social media, called on the UK government to “seize this opportunity to deliver a reset to children’s online safety”.“Andy Burnham has now seen that it is possible to take on big tech to address drivers of online harm,” a spokesperson said. “It’s time for the UK government to be brave, bold and decisive in ways it hasn’t been before.”Munira Wilson, who leads on children and families for the Liberal Democrats, said: “If a US court can pressure Meta into making significant changes to its platforms, why is our government still relying on optional curfews, strongly worded statements and unworkable bans?”Meanwhile, experts were sceptical that Meta’s agreed measures would tackle the underlying problems with the compulsive – some say addictive – app design that critics blame for social media harms.Dr Rachael Kent, a senior lecturer in digital economy and society education at King’s College London, said the settlement “does not fundamentally redesign the engagement-driven model. Some of the measures being introduced do not remove many of the underlying engagement mechanisms altogether – infinite scroll, autoplay and algorithmic recommendation remain – but introduce limits and stopping points around them.”Explore more on these topicsSocial media banMetaInternet safetyChildrenSocial mediaDigital mediaLaw (US)newsShareReuse this content

title: Cyborg cockroaches with tiny syringes designed to join search and rescue teams in major disasters | Robots | The Guardian
description: Giant burrowing cockroaches with added cameras and medical injectors are being tested as potential ‘first responders’ in earthquakes
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Giant burrowing cockroaches with added cameras and medical injectors are being tested as potential ‘first responders’ in earthquakes
Content: The research involved fitting the giant burrowing cockroach (Macropanesthia rhinoceros), with lightweight electronics and cameras.Photograph: PR imageView image in fullscreenThe research involved fitting the giant burrowing cockroach (Macropanesthia rhinoceros), with lightweight electronics and cameras.Photograph: PR imageRobotsCyborg cockroaches with tiny syringes designed to join search and rescue teams in major disastersGiant burrowing cockroaches with added cameras and medical injectors are being tested as potential ‘first responders’ in earthquakesFollow our Australia news live blog for latest updatesGet ourbreaking news email,free appordaily news podcastAustralian Associated PressWed 26 Aug 2026 21.16 EDTLast modified on Thu 27 Aug 2026 00.48 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFor people trapped under rubble in an earthquake or similar disaster, the arrival of a fleet of cockroaches could one day be the difference between life and death.Biorobotics engineers have been working on the design of six-legged cyborg insects with cameras and miniature medical injectors for search and rescue missions.The roaches are designed to deliveremergencyaid to people trapped in collapsed buildings, caves or other places too dangerous for rescuers to reach.The “paraborgs” have been developed by University ofQueenslandbiorobotics researchers, working with biomedical engineers at the University of New South Wales (UNSW).Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailUQ biorobotics engineer Thang Vo-Doan said their research transforms the cyborg insect from a mobile sensor into a tiny first responder, while critical medical decisions remain under human control.“Cyborg insects have been designed for search and explore missions for the past couple of decades,” Vo-Doan said.“We wanted to take the next step. Once they find someone, can they actually help?”Giant cyborg cockroaches designed to provide aid in search and rescue operations - videoThe research involved fitting a far north Queensland species, the giant burrowing cockroach (Macropanesthia rhinoceros), with lightweight electronics and cameras.They were also fitted with remotely activated auto-injection systems custom-made for the species.“Augmenting their natural biomechanics could allow these cyborg insects to deliver timely emergency assistance when direct access to people trapped in narrow, debris-filled spaces isn’t possible,” Vo-Doan said.View image in fullscreenThe cockroaches, like the team’s previous cyborg insect models, are anaesthetised during electrode and microchip fitting and live for as long as other cockroaches once the harnesses are removed.Photograph: PR imageIn proof-of-concept testing, the paraborgs achieved 95% success with close-range injection (positioned within 15cm of the target).The complete navigation-and-injection task succeeded in 72% of trials.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |When neededSign up toBreaking News AustraliaGet the most important news as it
